author: Ukrainian Cyber Alliance

description: Researchers at Kaspersky reveal that web pages hosting fake CATCHA checks are being used to propagate Lumma Stealer and Amadey, as part of a new ClickFix campaign.

author: APT29 a.k.a. BlueBravo, Cloaked Ursa, Cozy Bear, and Midnight Blizzard
target: Government, academia, defense, non-governmental organizations, and other sectors.
description: Researchers at Microsoft observe the Russian threat actor Midnight Blizzard sending a series of highly targeted spear-phishing emails to individuals in government, academia, defense, non-governmental organizations, and other sectors.

A network of 71 suspicious accounts on X is deployed ahead of the UN’s COP29 climate change conference. The accounts aim to give the impression of grassroots support for the Azerbaijan government, according to NGO Global Witness.
Threat actors hack Truth Terminal founder Andy Ayrey's social media account to promote a fraudulent token "IB."
Researchers at Trend Micro observe an attacker exploiting the Atlassian Confluence vulnerability CVE-2023-22527 to achieve remote code execution for cryptomining via the Titan Network.

description: Researchers at Palo Alto discover a ransomware incident where the threat actor Jumpy Pisces, tied to North Korea, collaborated with the Play ransomware group.
Researchers at Zimperium discover a new version of the FakeCall malware for Android able to hijack outgoing calls from a user to their bank, redirecting them to the attacker's phone number instead.
Researchers at Bitdefender uncover an ongoing malvertising campaign that abuses Meta's advertising platform and hijacked Facebook accounts to distribute an information stealer known as SYS01stealer.
Researchers at Cyble uncover a new variation of the Strela Stealer targeting Germany and Spain

Researchers at Sysdig discover a large-scale malicious operation named "EmeraldWhale" scanning for exposed Git configuration files to steal over 15,000 cloud account credentials from thousands of private repositories.

author: kzoldyck
description: ​Interbank, one of Peru's leading financial institutions, confirms a data breach after a threat actor who hacked into its systems leaked stolen data online.

Researchers at Checkmarx discover a new malicious Python package that masquerades as a cryptocurrency trading tool but harbors functionality designed to steal sensitive data and drain assets from victims' crypto wallets.

author: Emennet Pasargad a.k.a. Aria Sepehr Ayandehsazan, Cotton Sandstorm, Marnanbridge, and Haywire Kitten
description: U.S. and Israeli cybersecurity agencies attribute the Iranian cyber group Emennet Pasargad to targeting the 2024 Summer Olympics and compromising a French commercial dynamic display provider to show messages denouncing Israel's participation in the sporting event.

German pharmaceutical distributor AEP is hit with a ransomware attack.
Researchers at Human reveal that more than 1,000 legitimate shopping sites have been compromised to promote fake product listings in a credit card phishing scheme dubbed “Phish ‘n’ Ships,”

target: Facebook business and advertising account users in Taiwan
description: Researchers at Cisco Talos observe an unknown threat actor conducting a phishing campaign targeting Facebook business and advertising account users in Taiwan. The decoy email and fake PDF filenames are designed to impersonate a company's legal department, attempting to lure the victim into downloading and executing malware such as LummaC2 and Rhadamanthys.

target: Individuals in the U.S. and UK, Spain, Australia, and Japan.
description: Researchers at Netcraft reveal the details of Xiū gǒu, a new phishing kit used in campaigns targeting Australia, Japan, Spain, the U.K., and the U.S. since at least September 2024.

author: Storm-0940
description: Researchers at Microsoft warn that Chinese threat actors use the Quad7 botnet (a.k.a. CovertNetwork-1658 or xlogin), composed of hacked SOHO routers, to steal credentials in password-spray attacks.

author: Multiple threat actors from China including Volt Typhoon, APT31, and APT41/Winnti
description: Researchers at Sophos reveal that over the past five years, threat actors from China have increasingly used zero-day and known vulnerabilities to target edge networking devices from Fortinet, Barracuda, SonicWall, Check Point, D-Link, Cisco, Juniper, NetGear, Sophos, and many more.

Researchers at GreyNose reveal that threat actors are attempting to exploit CVE-2024-8956 and CVE-2024-8957, two zero-day vulnerabilities in PTZOptics pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) live streaming cameras used in industrial, healthcare, business conferences, government, and courtroom settings.
The popular LottieFiles Lotti-Player project is compromised in a supply chain attack to inject a crypto drainer into websites that steals visitors' cryptocurrency.

Researchers at Checkmarx, Phylum, and Socket discover independently an ongoing campaign targeting npm developers with hundreds of typosquat versions of their legitimate counterparts in an attempt to trick them into running cross-platform malware. The attack is notable for utilizing Ethereum smart contracts for command-and-control (C2) server address distribution.

LastPass warns about an ongoing campaign where scammers are writing reviews for its Chrome extension to promote a fake customer support phone number. However, this phone number is part of a much larger campaign to trick callers into giving scammers remote access to their computers.
The San Joaquin County Superior Court says that nearly all of its digital services are knocked offline due to a cyberattack.

Mystic Valley Elder Services suffers a data breach impacting many individuals.

A former worker hacked servers at Walt Disney World after being fired in order to manipulate computer menus by changing prices, adding profanities and altering notifications to wrongly declare some items as safe for people with allergies, according to a federal criminal complaint.

Australia's Western Sydney University said hackers breached its student management system and data warehouse to steal students' demographic and enrollment information in the third data theft incident of 2024.

author: Threat actors from Russia

France’s Ministry of Labor and Employment announces that it discovered a cyberattack against an unnamed service provider, and suspected to have impacted the data of young people it was helping get into employment.
Lampard Community School is hit by a cyber-attack and is being "blackmailed" by threat actors.
Threat actors compromise the centralized crypto exchange M2 to steal $13.7 million in assets, including Bitcoin, Ether and Solana.

author: Interlock

author: Embargo
description: Memorial Hospital and Manor posts an urgent message warning patients that the hospital’s IT team discovered a ransomware attack the morning before. The attack is claimed by the Embargo ransomware gang, which threatens to leak 1.15 terabytes of purportedly stolen data.
A threat actor steals over $4 million from crypto casino Metawin's Ethereum and Solana hot wallets

Google warns that CVE-2024-43047 and CVE-2024-43093, a security flaw impacting its Android operating system has come under active exploitation in the wild.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Atlanta Division issues an urgent warning to the public about a surge in cybercriminals exploiting “Remember-Me” cookies to gain unauthorized access to email accounts.
Researchers at Malwarebytes identify a new wave of phishing for banking credentials that targets consumers via Microsoft’s search engine.

author: Treat actors from China

author: Threat actors from North Korea

Researchers at Hunters discover an ongoing threat campaign dubbed VEILDrive taking advantage of legitimate services from Microsoft, including Teams, SharePoint, Quick Assist, and OneDrive, as part of its modus operandi.

author: Hellcat

author: IntelBroker

The information of over 300,000 Presbyterian Healthcare Services patients is compromised as a result of a data breach at law firm Thompson Coburn.

The FBI issues an alert to warn US-based companies and law enforcement agencies that threat actors are sending fake emergency data requests with the goal of harvesting personally identifiable information (PII).
Middlesbrough Council's website is affected by a distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack.

Researchers at Sophos discover a campaign targeting Bengal cat lovers in Australia with the Gootloader malware.

Researchers at Fortinet reveal that threat actors are increasingly targeting Windows users with the malicious Winos4.0 framework, distributed via seemingly benign game-related apps.
Researchers at Check Point reveal the details of CopyRh(ight)adamantys, an ongoing, large scale and sophisticated phishing campaign deploying the newest version of the Rhadamanthys stealer (0.7).
Researchers at Cyble identify a new variant of the GodFather malware, now targeting 500 banking and cryptocurrency apps.

Researchers at Kaspersky discover a new malicious package called 'SteelFox' able to mine cryptocurrency and steal credit card data by using the “bring your own vulnerable driver” technique to get SYSTEM privileges on Windows machines.
A cyberattack on Microlise leaves British prison vans without tracking systems or panic alarms.

More than 200,000 who shopped for blinds or window dressing this year had their credit card information and other data stolen after threat actors placed malware on the website of SelectBlinds, a major retailer.
The Houston Housing Authority falls victim of a ransomware attack.

description: Researchers from SentinelOne reveal the details of ‘Hidden Risk’, a campaign orchestrated by BlueNoroff, a threat actor with ties to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) targeting cryptocurrency-related businesses with a multi-stage malware capable of infecting Apple macOS devices.

Researchers at Perception Point discover threat actors distributing malware disguised as a legitimate shipping document, and delivering the malicious payload as a concatenated ZIP file attached to an email, designed to bypass detection in most standard ZIP readers while targeting Windows and WinRAR users.

description: Researchers at Cado Security discover a GuLoader campaign targeting European industrial and engineering companies.

Researchers at CYFIRMA identify “Wish Stealer,” a new Node.js-based malware that targets Windows users by stealing sensitive information from Discord, web browsers, cryptocurrency wallets, and social media accounts.

author: Vizor

Researchers at Fortinet uncover a dangerous phishing campaign distributing a new Remcos RAT variant exploiting the CVE-2017-0199 vulnerability to download and execute an HTML Application (HTA) file.

Researchers at Socket detect five malicious npm packages specifically targeting Roblox users, and designed to impersonate legitimate modules widely used within the Roblox developer community. The threat actor published typosquatted packages to deceive developers into installing Skuld infostealer and Blank Grabber malware.
Researchers at Malwarebytes discover a Fakebat (a.k.a. Eugenloader, PaykLoader) campaign where the malware is distributed via a malicious Google ad for the productivity application Notion.

Newpark Resources, a key supplier for oilfields says a ransomware attack caused disruptions and limited access to certain systems.
Ahold Delhaize, the Dutch parent company of Stop & Shop, Hannaford, Food Lion, and Giant Food releases a statement warning that it recently discovered a cyberattack within its U.S. network.

The FBI and several Black political leaders warn the public about a string of offensive text messages sent to African Americans across the U.S. following former President Donald Trump’s win in the 2024 presidential election.
Debt relief solutions provider Forth (Set Forth) notifies 1.5 million individuals that their personal information was compromised in a May 2024 data breach.
A coordinated IP spoofing attack attempts to disrupt the Tor anonymity network, according to the Tor Project and relay operators.

Researchers at Rapid7 observe an ongoing malware campaign involving a new version of LodaRAT with the ability to steal cookies and passwords from Microsoft Edge and Brave.

The Virginia Attorney General’s Office is struck by a cyberattack that forces officials off the office’s computer systems.
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

author: Unknown Threat Actor(s)
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-24200 Apple iOS and iPadOS Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

Researchers at Rapid7 reveal that the threat actors who were behind the exploitation of a zero-day vulnerability in BeyondTrust Privileged Remote Access (PRA) and Remote Support (RS) products in December 2024 likely also exploited CVE-2025-1094, a previously unknown SQL injection flaw in PostgreSQL.

author: REF7707 a.k.a. CL-STA-0049
target: Governments, Defense, Telecommunication, Education and Aviation sectors in Southeast Asia and South America
description: Researchers from Elastic and Palo Alto Networks disclose the details of a new campaign from Chinese-speaking threat actors, targeting governments, defense, telecommunication,education and aviation sectors in Southeast Asia and South America with a malware strain called FINALDRAFT capable of granting remote access to infected hosts.

author: Emperor Dragonfly
description: Researchers from Symantec reveal that a China-based threat actor, tracked as Emperor Dragonfly and commonly associated with cybercriminal endeavors, has been observed using Korplug, a toolset previously attributed to espionage actors, in a RA World ransomware attack.

author: Kimsuky, a.k.a. APT43, Black Banshee, Emerald Sleet, Sparkling Pisces, Springtail, TA427, and Velvet Chollima.
target: South Korean Business, Government, and Cryptocurrency Sectors
description: Researcher at Securonix unveil the details of DEEP#DRIVE, a campaign by the North Korean threat actor Kimsuky targeting South Korean business, government, and cryptocurrency sectors.

author: Salt Typhoon a.k.a. RedMike
target: Five Telecommunications Firms in the U.S.
description: Researchers at Recorded Future reveal that the Chinese government-linked hacking group, Salt Typhoon, is continuing to compromise telecommunications providers in the U.S. exploiting two vulnerabilities (tracked as CVE-2023-20198 and CVE-2023-20273) to compromise unpatched Cisco devices running Cisco IOS XE software.

author: Storm-2372
target: Government, non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), Information Technology (IT) Services and Technology, Defense, Telecommunications, Health, Higher Education, and Energy/Oil and Gas sectors in Europe, North America, Africa, and the Middle East.
description: Researchers at Microsoft unveil an emerging threat cluster of Russian origin, dubbed Storm-2372 attributed to a new set of cyber attacks aimed at a variety of sectors since August 2024, using the 'device code phishing' technique.

author: Threat Actors from Russia
description: Researchers from Volexity identify several social-engineering and spear-phishing campaigns by Russian threat actors aimed at compromising Microsoft 365 (M365) accounts, using the 'device code phishing' technique.

author: Mustang Panda
description: Researchers at ClearSky reveal to have discovered a UI vulnerability in Microsoft Windows, actively exploited by a suspected Chinese APT group - Mustang Panda.

author: PurpleBravo (threat actor from North Korea a.k.a. CL-STA-0240, Famous Chollima, and Tenacious Pungsan)
target: At least seven entities, three of which are in the cryptocurrency sector, including a market-making firm, an online casino, and a software company.
description: Researchers at Recorded Future discover a new wave of attacks from the Contagious Interview campaign targeting at least seven entities, three of which are in the cryptocurrency sector, including a market-making firm, an online casino, and a software company.

author: EarthKapre, a.k.a. RedCurl
target: Private-sector Organizations, especially in the Law Firms & Legal Services Industry
description: Researchers at eSentire unveil a new campaign from the group EarthKapre, also referred to as RedCurl, targeting private-sector organizations, particularly those in the Law Firms & Legal Services industry, using a legitimate Adobe executable (ADNotificationManager.exe) to sideload the EarthKapre/RedCurl loader.

author: Winnti, overlapping with Earth Freybug, a subset of APT41, a.k.a. CuckooBees, and Blackfly.
target: Japanese Companies in the Manufacturing, Materials, and Energy Sectors
description: Researchers at LAC attribute the China-linked threat actor known as Winnti to a new campaign dubbed RevivalStone that targeted Japanese companies in the manufacturing, materials, and energy sectors in March 2024.

author: Jurak
description: A threat actor named Jurak publishes data samples on a hacker forum, claiming a breach at Zacks Investment Research in June 2024 that exposed data of 12 millions of customers.
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

description: Researchers at Cyfirma discover a campaign distributing stealer malware via obfuscated JavaScript files to harvest a wide range of sensitive data from compromised Windows systems and exfiltrate it to a Telegram bot.

author: Multiple Threat Actors
target: Multiple Organizations in the UAV and counter-UAV sector
description: Researchers at Resecurity detect a rise in cyberattacks targeting UAV and counter-UAV technologies.

Italian spyware maker SIO, known to sell its products to government customers, is behind Spyrtacus, a spyware embedded in a series of malicious Android apps that masquerade as WhatsApp and other popular apps but steal private data from a target’s device.

author: "Tooda"
description: A threat actor with the moniker "Tooda" leaks 136,000+ user records, emails, and a ‘blacklist’ file, exposing those who paid to keep their info off the doxxing platform.

Researchers at Sucuri discover an incident involving a WordPress site that leveraged the mu-plugins (or must-use plugins) directory to implant backdoors and execute malicious PHP code in a stealthy manner.
Researchers at Cofense discover a phishing campaign leveraging a fake 'Adobe Drive X' app to steal Microsoft Login credentials.
Researchers at CloudSEK discover a large-scale Search Engine Poisoning (SEP) campaign that targets Indian government, educational, and financial websites.

author: Threat Actors from Russia
description: Researchers at Netskope shed light on a new Golang-based backdoor that uses Telegram as a mechanism for command-and-control (C2) communications.

author: “Nam3l3ess"
description: PPL Electric Utilities, a Pennsylvania utility company says that basic customer data stolen from one of its vendors in 2023, via the MOVEit file transfer software vulnerability, was recently exposed online, but the incident did not affect its core systems.
Cybersecurity researchers at Veriti discovere a campaign targeting the release of declassified JFK (John F. Kennedy), RFK (Robert F. Kennedy Jr.), and MLK (Martin Luther King Jr.) files.

author: Author
description: Description
Researchers at Microsoft discover a new variant of a known Apple macOS malware called XCSSET as part of limited attacks in the wild.

author: NoName057(16)
target: Several Italian organizations, including Intesa San Paolo bank, Milan's Linate and Malpensa airports, the Transport Authority, and ports of Taranto and Trieste.
description: Pro-Russia hacker group, NoName057(16), launches DDoS attacks against Italian banks and airports. The attacks are a response to Italy's support for Ukraine, as stated by the group on their Telegram channel.

Ecuador's National Assembly reports two cyberattacks aimed at disrupting its systems and accessing sensitive data. The attacks happened a week after the country's general election. The assembly counteracted the situation but provided no further details. The country's national civil registry and election agency have also been recently targeted by similar attacks.
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

author: TA2726 and TA2727
description: Researchers at Proofpoint discover a new campaign that leverages web injects to deliver a new Apple macOS malware known as FrigidStealer.

author: Mustang Panda a.k.a. Earth Preta, Stately Taurus
description: Researchers from Trend Micro observe the Chinese state-sponsored threat actor known as Mustang Panda employing a novel technique to evade detection and maintain control over infected systems, involving the use of a legitimate Microsoft Windows utility called Microsoft Application Virtualization Injector (MAVInject.exe) to inject the threat actor's malicious payload into an external process, waitfor.exe, whenever ESET antivirus application is detected running.

target: Gamers who downloaded pirated versions of games
description: Researchers at Kaspersky discover StaryDobry, a campaign carried out by a threat actor distributing malicious, cracked games via torrents. The games contained a cryptominer that was activated at the end of 2024 and affected both personal and corporate users.

target: Windows users located in China, Turkey, Indonesia, Taiwan, and Spain.
description: Researchers at Fortinet discover a new variant of the Snake Keylogger malware used to actively target Windows users located in China, Turkey, Indonesia, Taiwan, and Spain and leveraging AutoIT to evade detection.

author: NailaoLocker
target: European Organizations in the Healthcare Sector
description: Researchers from Orange Cyberdefense reveal the details of Green Nailao, a previously unknown threat activity cluster targeted European organizations, particularly those in the healthcare sector, to deploy PlugX and its successor, ShadowPad, with the intrusions ultimately leading to deployment of a ransomware called NailaoLocker.

A new malware campaign, identified by AhnLab, distributes info-stealers such as Lumma and ACR Stealer through malicious installers disguised as cracked software. The attack uses a "dead drop resolver" technique to extract the command-and-control server and steals a wide range of sensitive data for profit.

Researchers from reveal another campaign that uses files with the extension "MSC," which can be executed by the Microsoft Management Console (MMC), to deliver the Rhadamanthys stealer malware, exploiting the vulnerability of apds.dll (CVE-2024-43572), or executing the 'command' command using Console Taskpad.

target: Affiliates of a major American political action committee (PAC)
description: Researchers at Juniper discover a phishing attack using invisible Unicode characters to hide malicious JavaScript. The attack targeted a major American political action committee and used personalized links and other evasion techniques.

date_occurred_raw: Since at least 2023, with usage peaking in 2024.
author: CryptoBytes (a Russian threat group)
description: Researchers at SonicWall Capture Labs discover that the financially motivated Russian cybercriminal group CryptoBytes is still active with the UxCryptor ransomware, often bundled with other malware. The group, active since 2023, uses leaked ransomware builders.

Researchers at ESET discover an email scam that exploits fears of job loss by sending fake termination notices. The phishing emails trick recipients into clicking malicious links or opening attachments, which can lead to data theft or malware downloads.

author: BlackLock a.k.a. El Dorado
description: Researchers at ReliaQuest details BlackLock, a RaaS operator first observed in March 2024, that uses a double extortion tactic and custom malware to target Windows, VMWare ESXi, and Linux environments.
A highly obfuscated .NET Remote Access Trojan (RAT), also known as sectopRAT, masquerades as a Google Chrome extension named "Google Docs" to deceive users into installing it.

Researchers at Hunt.io discover an attack campaign targeting Chinese-speaking users with backdoored installers for popular apps like Signal, LINE, and Gmail. The attackers used fraudulent download pages that looked legitimate, tricking victims into downloading the malicious software.

author: Xelera
description: Researchers at Seqrite Labs discover a campaign targeting job seekers in India with fake job offers from Food Corporations of India. The attack uses malicious documents to deploy Xelera ransomware and a Discord bot to steal data and disrupt systems.
Researchers at Cofense warn about a new phishing attack that uses fake emails claiming their Prime subscriptions will be auto-renewed at an unexpected price to steal login and payment information.

Venture capital giant Insight Partners is hit by a sophisticated social engineering attack. The attack gained unauthorized access to their information systems, potentially compromising banking, tax, and personal data.

A security breach affects thousands of wallets connected to Cardex, a blockchain-based game. The attack, identified as a "session key hack," allows a malicious actor to exploit a compromised session signer wallet shared by all Cardex users. A leaked key in Cardex's frontend code enabled the attacker to conduct unauthorized transactions, draining $400,000 from 9,000 wallets.

author: Multiple Russia-aligned threat actors including UNC5792, UNC4221, Sandworm (a.k.a. APT44), Turla, and UNC1151
description: Researchers at Google reveal that multiple Russia-aligned threat actors have been observed targeting individuals of interest via the privacy-focused messaging app Signal to gain unauthorized access to their accounts.

date_occurred_raw: Beginning in early 2021, and as recently as January 2025
author: Ghost, a.k.a. Cring
target: Critical infrastructure, schools and universities, healthcare, government networks, religious institutions, technology, and manufacturing companies
description: A joint advisory by CISA and the FBI warns about "Ghost" ransomware, which has been active since early 2021. The China-based cybercriminals target outdated software and firmware to breach organizations across more than 70 countries for financial gain. The attack, also known as Cring, affects sectors like critical infrastructure, healthcare, and government networks.

author: North Korea's cyber-espionage campaign, "Contagious Interview."
description: Researchers at Kandj uncover the DriverEasy malware, which pretends to be a Chrome update. It steals user passwords and sends them via Dropbox's API. This malware is linked to North Korea's "Contagious Interview" campaign.

Researchers at Any.run discover Zhong Stealer, a malware exploiting customer support platforms like Zendesk, and using social engineering to trick support staff into downloading malicious files and exfiltrating sensitive data.

author: Termite
description: An Australian fertility services provider, Genea, is hit by a security breach where an unauthorized third party accessed Genea's network and data.

target: Private sector business executives (in finance, logistics, real estate), a European government official, and civil society members.
description: New findings from iVerify have detect Pegasus spyware on several private sector phones. The zero-click spyware is reportedly more widespread, now targeting business executives in addition to civil society. This marks a new dimension to the spyware crisis as these individuals hold access to sensitive corporate and financial data.
A business email compromise (BEC) scheme against mining company NioCorp results in a loss of $500,000 in misdirected vendor payments, after threat actors breached its information and email systems.

author: Mustang Panda a.k.a. Earth Preta, Stately Taurus
description: Researchers at Palo Alto Networks unveil a new campaign by Mustang Panda, targeting organizations in Myanmar using the Bookworm malware.

author: NailaoLocker
target: At least 21 companies across 15 countries in Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and South America, primarily in Manufacturing, Transportation, and Publishing
description: Researchers from Trend Micro observe the updated Shadowpad malware being used to deploy the NailaoLocker ransomware after exploiting weak passwords and bypassing multi-factor authentication.

author: Threat Actors from North Korea
description: Researchers from ESET reveal the details of DeceptiveDevelopment, a campaign carried out by threat actors linked to North Korea, where the operators, posing as headhunters, try to serve their targets with software projects that conceal infostealing malware

author: Unknown Threat Actor(s)
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-23209, a vulnerability in the Craft content management system (CMS) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.

target: Individuals searching for Google Chrome online
description: Malwarebytes researchers discover the Sectoprat remote access trojan (RAT) being distributed via malicious Google Ads and a fake Google Chrome installer, which targeted users searching for the browser.

date_occurred_raw: Multi-year period, with activity observed as early as 2019 and a significant campaign in late 2024 and early 2025
author: Salt Typhoon (a.k.a. UNC2286, GhostEmperor, and Earth Estries)
target: U.S. telecom providers (e.g., AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, Lumen, etc.).
description: Researchers at Cisco Talos reveal that Salt Typhoon, a Chinese state-sponsored group, used custom JumbledPath malware and stolen credentials to infiltrate U.S. telecom providers for cyberespionage.

author: ExploitWhispers
description: An unknown threat actor dubbed ExploitWhispers releases what they claim to be an archive of internal Matrix chat logs belonging to the Black Basta ransomware operation.
Researchers at Source Defense discover a payment card skimming campaign using a malicious script to replace checkout forms and leverage the Stripe API to validate and steal credit card data.

Researchers at Bitdefender Labs discover the "streamjacking" campaign targeting the CS2 community. The attack involves threat actors impersonating professional players on hijacked YouTube channels and using fake giveaways to steal Steam accounts and cryptocurrency from unsuspecting gamers.

author: ScreamedJungle
target: Over 115 e-commerce sites running on the Magento platform
description: Researchers at Group-IB discover the ScreamedJungle campaign, which injects malicious JavaScript into vulnerable Magento websites to steal browser fingerprints from users.

author: Cyber Alliance
description: A pro-Ukraine hacking group, Cyber Alliance, claims responsibility for a cyberattack on Russian microfinance company CarMoney, which destroyed its infrastructure and allegedly compromised customer data.

author: Medusa
description: UK healthcare provider HCRG Care Group confirms a data breach after the Medusa ransomware group claims to have stolen over two terabytes of sensitive data and demanded a ransom.

Fashion Box S.p.A., the Italian parent company of Replay Jeans, is hit by a cyberattack. A threat actor used a brute force attack to access the company's servers, exfiltrating confidential and personal data, including stakeholder information.

author: RansomHouse
description: The RansomHouse group claims responsibility for stealing data from the Supreme Administrative Court’s information systems.
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

author: Lazarus Group
description: Cryptocurrency exchange Bybit reveals that a "sophisticated" attack led to the theft of over $1.5 billion worth of cryptocurrency from one of its Ethereum cold (offline) wallets, making it the largest ever single crypto heist in history.

author: Unknown Threat Actor(s)
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-24989, a Microsoft Power Pages Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

author: Sticky Werewolf a.k.a. Angry Likho
description: Researches at Kaspersky link the threat actor known as Sticky Werewolf to targeted attacks primarily in Russia and Belarus with the aim of delivering the Lumma Stealer malware by means of a previously undocumented implant.

author: Chinese-speaking threat actors (suspected)
description: Researchers from CYFIRMA discover SpyLend, an Android app on Google Play, that was downloaded 100,000 times. It masqueraded as a finance app to steal user data for blackmail and extortion.

target: Websites running WordPress and their visitors
description: Researchers at Sucuri discover a new reCAPTCHA malware campaign on WordPress sites that presents fake browser update warnings. It tricks visitors into executing a malicious PowerShell script to install trojans and information stealers on their computers.

author: Portuguese-speaking threat actor
description: Researchers at Cyble discover that a threat actor is using the open-source tool Null-AMSI to bypass security features and deploy AsyncRAT via a malicious LNK file disguised as a wallpaper.

author: Storm-1516 (threat Actors from Russia)
description: Germany’s security services warn that fake videos circulating online purporting to reveal ballot manipulation in the country’s upcoming federal elections are part of a Russian information operation.

Siberia's largest dairy plant, Semyonishna, is hit by a LockBit variant ransomware attack. The attackers used the remote access software AnyDesk and targeted systems that reportedly lacked antivirus protection. The attack disrupted the plant's ability to label products but did not affect milk processing. The motivation appears to be a protest against the company's support for Russian troops in Ukraine.

author: APT41 (a.k.a. Winnti) suspected
target: Manufacturers, particularly in the aviation and aerospace industries.
description: Check Point researchers discover that APT41 exploited CVE-2024-24919, a path traversal vulnerability in their security gateways to gain initial access to dozens of OT organizations globally. The threat actors then deployed the modular ShadowPad backdoor to steal valuable intellectual property.
country: US MX Europe Middle East, Africa

description: Niva Bupa Health Insurance is investigating a data leak after an anonymous sender claimed to have customer data. The company informs exchanges, while no ransomware group has publicly claimed responsibility for the alleged breach.

A PayPal email scam exploits the platform's address feature to send fake purchase notifications. The emails, from "service@paypal.com," claim a new address was added for a high-value item and provide a fake support number. The goal is to trick users into installing remote access software.

author: Hacktivist groups that support Ukraine (suspected)
target: LANIT, a major Russian IT service and software provider. Specifically, its subsidiaries LLC LANTER and LLC LAN ATMservice
description: Russia's National Coordination Center for Computer Incidents (NKTsKI) discloses a hack at LANIT, a major Russian IT service provider, prompting a warning to the financial sector to change passwords and credentials.

Rubrik discloses a breach on a log server that led to the exposure of some authentication keys. The company rotates the keys as a precautionary measure, stating there was no evidence of unauthorized access to customer data or internal code.

author: UAC-0212
target: Supplier Companies from Serbia, the Czech Republic, and Ukraine
description: Researchers from CERT-UA attribute a sub-cluster within the Sandworm hacking group (aka APT44, Seashell Blizzard, and UAC-0002) to the exploitation of a now-patched security flaw in Microsoft Windows (CVE-2024-38213) via booby-trapped documents.

Researchers at the Shadowserver Foundation discover a large-scale brute force password attack using almost 2.8 million IP addresses and attempting to guess the credentials for a wide range of networking devices, including those from Palo Alto Networks, Ivanti, and SonicWall.
country: AR BR RU TR MA MX

description: Anne Arundel County discloses a security incident and warns residents that multiple services are still down.
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

author: Unknown Threat Actor(s)
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2017-3066, a deserialization vulnerability impacting Adobe ColdFusion to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.

author: Unknown Threat Actor(s)
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2024-20953, a deserialization vulnerability impacting Oracle Agile PLM, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.

author: Chinese-speaking threat actors
target: Government agencies and industrial organizations, particularly manufacturing, construction, information technology, telecommunications, healthcare, power and energy, and large-scale logistics and transportation, in Taiwan, Malaysia, China, Japan, Thailand, South Korea, Singapore, the Philippines, Vietnam, and Hong Kong.
description: Researchers at Kaspersky reveal the details of Operation SalmonSlalom, a campaign against various industrial organizations in the Asia-Pacific (APAC) region, designed to deliver a known malware called FatalRAT, and abusing legitimate Chinese cloud content delivery network (CDN) myqcloud and the Youdao Cloud Notes.
Researchers at Kaspersky warn of an ongoing campaign, dubbed GitVenom, that's targeting gamers and cryptocurrency investors under the guise of open-source projects hosted on GitHub.

author: Silver Fox?
description: Researchers at Check Point reveal the details of a large-scale malware campaign leveraging a vulnerable Windows driver associated with Adlice's product suite to sidestep detection efforts and deliver the Gh0st RAT malware.

author: Unattributed Chinese-affiliated Group
target: Microsoft 365 Accounts Across Various Industries in finance, healthcare, government, and education
description: Researchers at SecurityScorecard discover a botnet campaign using over 130,000 compromised devices to perform password-spraying attacks on Microsoft 365 accounts, bypassing MFA by exploiting non-interactive sign-ins and Basic Authentication.

target: Universities and Government Organizations in North America
description: Researchers at Palo Alto Networks reveal that universities and government organizations in North America and Asia have been targeted by a previously undocumented Linux malware called Auto-Color

author: Chinese-speaking threat actor
description: Researchers at Intel471 discover an updated version of an Android malware called TgToxic (a.k.a. ToxicPanda), indicating that the threat actors behind it are continuously making changes in response to public reporting.

author: Space Pirates
description: Researchers at Solar link the threat actor known as Space Pirates to a malicious campaign targeting Russian information technology organizations with a previously undocumented malware called LuckyStrike Agent in a campaign dubbed Erudite Mogwai.

author: LockBit
description: A LockBit ransomware attack exploits a critical vulnerability (CVE-2023-22527) in an unpatched Confluence server to gain initial access. The threat actor then performed reconnaissance, moved laterally across the network using tools like RDP and Mimikatz, and ultimately deployed the ransomware.

date_discovered_raw: First observed in November 2024, with a new variant in February 2025
author: LCRYX
description: Researchers at K7 discover a new wave of attacks launched by the LCRYX ransomware gang.
A novel malware delivery framework is detected that uses a batch script with AI-assisted obfuscation to bypass security and install either XWorm or AsyncRAT, complicating detection.

author: Silver Fox, a.k.a. Void Arachne and The Great Thief of Valley
target: Healthcare organizations, specifically those using Philips DICOM viewers
description: Researchers at Forescout discover a campaign by the Chinese threat actor Silver Fox, which abused Philips DICOM viewers to deploy a backdoor, a keylogger, and a crypto miner on victim computers, suggesting an expansion of their targeting to new regions.

Threat actors steal $49 million from Hong Kong-based stablecoin neobank Infini. The breach stemmed from compromised administrative privileges, enabling the attacker to manipulate the contract settings and siphon funds. Infini acknowledges the security breach.

author: UAC-0173
description: The Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) warns of renewed activity from an organized criminal group it tracks as UAC-0173 that involves infecting computers with a remote access trojan named DCRat (aka DarkCrystal RAT).
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

date_occurred_raw: Since at least the end of 2023.
description: Researchers at Sekoia discover a new malware campaign targeting edge devices from Cisco, ASUS, QNAP, and Synology to rope them into a botnet named PolarEdge.
Researchers at Socket uncover a malicious PyPI package exploiting Deezer’s API to enable coordinated music piracy through API abuse and C2 server control.

date_occurred_raw: Multi-year period, with activity observed as early as 2019 and a significant campaign in late 2024 and early 2025
author: Salt Typhoon (a.k.a. UNC2286, GhostEmperor, and Earth Estries)
target: Telecommunications Companies, Government Agencies, and Universities.
description: Researchers at GreyNoise observe exploitation of CVE-2018-0171, the vulnerability used in a recent attack by the China-backed threat group Salt Typhoon

author: Multiple Threat Actors
target: Individuals and a wide range of services, including social media, financial institutions, and government domains.
description: Have I Been Pwned adds over 284 million accounts stolen by infostealer malware to its database. The data, from a collection called "ALIEN TXTBASE" shared on a Telegram channel, contains email addresses, passwords, and other credentials from infected individual devices.

Researchers from McAfee Labs discover a phishing campaign using fake video links and social engineering to redirect users through multiple malicious websites, ultimately leading to the download of a malicious MSI file.

Cybersecurity researchers discover the Poseidon Mac malware, which hides within PKG files and uses preinstall scripts to deliver its malicious payload, stealing sensitive data from unsuspecting users.

author: Ghostwriter (aka Moonscape, TA445, UAC-0057, and UNC1151)
target: Opposition Activists in Belarus as well as Ukrainian Military and Government Organizations
description: Researchers at Sentinel One discover a new campaign employing malware-laced Microsoft Excel documents as lures to deliver a new variant of PicassoLoader.

author: Unknown Threat Actor(s)
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2024-49035, an improper access control vulnerability in Microsoft Partner Center to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

author: Unknown Threat Actor(s)
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2023-34192, a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Synacor ZCS to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

author: Rey, part of the HellCat ransomware group.
description: Orange Group confirms a cyberattack on its Romanian branch after a threat actor known as "Rey" leaks company documents. The attacker claims to have stolen thousands of internal documents and user records after accessing a non-critical back-office application.

A data breach at US drug testing firm DISA Global Solutions impacts 3.3 million people. The breach occurred between February and April 2024. While the attack method is unknown, a ransom was reportedly paid.

author: Anubis
description: Researchers at Kela reveal that Pound Road Medical Centre (PRMC) was a target of the Anubis Ransomware-as-a-Service operation.

author: Anubis
description: Researchers at Kela reveal that Summit Home Health was a target of the Anubis Ransomware-as-a-Service operation.

author: Anubis
description: Researchers at Kela reveal that Comercializadora S&E Perú, a Peru-based company from the engineering & construction sector, was a target of the Anubis Ransomware-as-a-Service operation.

author: Anubis
target: US-based Firm from the Engineering & Construction Sector
description: Researchers at Kela reveal that a US-based firm from the engineering & construction Sector, was a target of the Anubis Ransomware-as-a-Service operation.

target: Cryptocurrency Users of AI tools like DeepSeek
description: Researchers at Zscaler uncover a cybercrime campaign impersonating DeepSeek AI to distribute malware. The attackers used brand impersonation, fake CAPTCHAs, and clipboard injection to trick users into executing malicious PowerShell commands and downloading the Vidar information stealer.

target: Over 350 websites, including government portals, U.S. state government sites, American universities, major hotel chains, news outlets, car dealerships, and several Fortune 500 companies.
description: A cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Krpano, a virtual tour framework, is weaponized by malicious actors in a campaign dubbed 360XSS, to inject malicious scripts across hundreds of websites with the goal of manipulating search results and fueling a spam ads campaign at scale.
Researchers at Sucuri discover a fake WordPress plugin that was injecting casino spam into the footer of a client's website to manipulate search engine rankings and drive traffic to malicious sites.

author: Crazy Evil
target: Job seekers in the Web3 and crypto sector, cryptocurrency wallet holders.
description: Security researchers discover that the Crazy Evil group targeted Web3 job seekers with fake interviews, tricking them into downloading a malicious application called GrassCall, which steals cryptocurrency.

author: China-linked Threat Actors
description: An internal audit by Belgium's State Security Service (VSSE) reveals that China-linked threat actors stole 10% of their emails. The attack exploited a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2023-2868) in a Barracuda Email Security Gateway (ESG) appliance, exposing sensitive information from 2021 to May 2023.
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

author: Exodus Security
description: A threat actor dubbed Exodus Security claims responsibility for breaching the Philippine Army's networks and accessing confidential documents, though the army claims the attack was contained and no data was stolen.
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

description: Pump.fun's X account is hacked to promote a scam governance token. A fake "PUMP" token and another named "GPT-4.5" are promoted from the compromised account. The platform warns users on its Telegram channel not to interact with the hacked X account.
A cyber incident shuts down the Cleveland Municipal Court. The court remained closed for at least three days, with officials stating they had not yet confirmed the nature and scope of the event.
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

author: Qilin
description: The Health Ministry of Palau experiences a ransomware attack from the Qilin ransomware group. The attack compromised patient data from the Belau National Hospital.

author: Silver Fox?
description: Researchers at Fortinet discover a new campaign targeting companies in Taiwan with malware known as Winos 4.0 as part of phishing emails masquerading as the country's National Taxation Bureau.

Researchers at Netskope uncover a widespread phishing campaign that uses fake CAPTCHA images shared via PDF documents hosted on Webflow's content delivery network to deliver the Lumma stealer malware.

Researchers at QiAnXin XLab, discover a campaign that has infected Android TV devices with a botnet malware dubbed Vo1d, with the botnet scaling a peak of 1,590,299 on January 19, 2025, spanning 226 countries and regions.

author: Lotus Panda a.k.a. Billbug, Bronze Elgin, Lotus Blossom, Spring Dragon, and Thrip
target: Manufacturing, Telecommunications, and Media Sectors in the Philippines, Vietnam, Hong Kong, and Taiwan
description: Researchers at Cisco Talos discover a campaign carried out by the threat actor known as Lotus Panda targeting government, manufacturing, telecommunications, and media sectors in the Philippines, Vietnam, Hong Kong, and Taiwan with updated versions of a known backdoor called Sagerunex.

author: EncryptHub, a.k.a. Larva-208
description: Prodaft discover the EncryptHub threat group, also known as Larva-208, which has been active since June 2024. The financially motivated group uses phishing and social engineering to breach over 600 organizations, deploying infostealers and ransomware.

Security researchers identify a malware campaign distributing a Python-based stealer called Redox. The attackers used social engineering with fake mods and cracks on GitHub to steal sensitive user data.

Researchers at Malwarebytes identify a new scam targeting PayPal customers with very convincing ads and pages. Crooks are abusing both Google and PayPal’s infrastructure in order to trick victims calling for assistance to speak with fraudsters instead.

author: Mustang Panda
description: Researchers at Cado Security Labs uncover a new malware campaign targeting the Royal Thai Police with the Yokai backdoor, attributed to the Chinese APT group Mustang Panda.
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

author: Suspected Chinese threat actor (CL-STA-0049)
target: Governments, Defense, Telecommunication, Education and Aviation Sectors in Southeast Asia and South America.
description: Researchers at Palo Alto Networks discover a suspected Chinese threat actor, CL-STA-0049, using a multi-platform backdoor, Squidoor, to target various sectors in Southeast Asia and South America by exploiting vulnerabilities in IIS servers and deploying web shells.

author: DragonForce
description: Researchers at Resecurity report that the DragonForce ransomware is recently targeting organizations in Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) with a significant incident involving Al Bawani, a prominent Riyadh real estate and construction company.

Researchers at Microsoft reveal that threat actors have been exploiting CVE-2025-0289, a security vulnerability in Paragon Partition Manager's BioNTdrv.sys driver in ransomware attacks to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code.

author: JavaGhost a.k.a. TGR-UNK-0011
description: Researchers at Palo Alto Networks reveal the details of TGR-UNK-0011, a threat actor targeting Amazon Web Services (AWS) environments to push out phishing campaigns to unsuspecting targets.

target: Internet Service Providers in China and the West Coast of the U.S.
description: Researchers at Splunk discover a campaign targeting Internet service providers (ISPs) in China and the West Coast of the United States, and deploying information stealers and cryptocurrency miners on compromised hosts.
Over 3.2 million Google Chrome users are at risk after threat actors hijack popular browser extensions, injecting malicious scripts and redirecting web traffic for fraud.

author: Eleven11bot (Iran-linked botnet)
description: Researchers from Nokia Deepfield and GreyNoise identify a large, persistent botnet that is launching DDoS attacks and brute-force attacks on IoT devices using weak and default passwords.

author: Dark Caracal (a.k.a. ATK27, TAG-CT3, G0070).
target: Organizations in various sectors, including mining, manufacturing, and hospitality in South America
description: Researchers at Positive Technologies discover that the Dark Caracal group has been using new malware, Poco RAT, to target Spanish-speaking individuals since 2022, primarily through phishing emails.
Franklin County discloses to be dealing with a ransomware attack.
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

description: Missouri’s Department of Conservation is facing outages from a cyberattack.
target_class: Public admin and defence, social security

author: Serbian Authorities
description: Amnesty International discovered that Serbian authorities used CVE-2024-53104, a Cellebrite zero-day exploit, to gain physical access to a student activist's Android phone, bypass the lock screen, and install spyware during detention.

A cyberattack targets Indian stock brokerage firm Angel One, resulting in a data breach of client information stored in its Amazon Web Services (AWS) account. The company's shares drops significantly after the announcement.

description: Description

author: Unknown
target: Users of ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and general Chrome browser users
description: Researchers discover two malicious Chrome extensions, "Chat GPT for Chrome" and "AI Sidebar," exfiltrating ChatGPT and DeepSeek conversations and affecting 900,000 users.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at CloudSEK unveil the RondoDox botnet, a campaign that leverages the React2Shell vulnerability (CVE-2025-55182), to hijack unpatched servers and IoT hardware.

author: TridentLocker
description: Sedgwick discovers a ransomware attack on its government subsidiary Sedgwick Government Solutions's isolated file transfer system. The incident, claimed by the TridentLocker gang, involved the theft of 3.4 GB of data.

author: APT36 (a.k.a. Transparent Tribe)
target: Indian government, academic, and strategic institutions
description: Researchers at Cyfirma discover a cyber-espionage campaign where APT36 used spear-phishing emails containing ZIP archives delivering "ReadOnly" and "WriteOnly" malware, allowing the attackers to bypass antivirus, exfiltrate sensitive data, monitor clipboards, and maintain long-term surveillance over Indian government and military-linked organizations to serve state intelligence goals.

author: Qilin (a.k.a. Agenda)
description: The Qilin ransomware group attacks Covenant Health. Initially reported as a minor breach, investigations revealed that sensitive medical and personal data of nearly 480,000 individuals were compromised. The attack severely disrupted hospital operations, forcing reliance on manual paper processes for weeks.

author: French-speaking threat actor; active in Telegram groups such as "Myth Stеaler" and "Еуes Steаlеr GC."
target: Discord users, including those using Chromium-based and Firefox browsers.
description: Researchers at Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 discover VVS Stealer, a Python-based infostealer using Pyarmor obfuscation to bypass security tools. The malware steals Discord tokens, injects malicious JavaScript to hijack sessions, harvests browser credentials, and maintains persistence on Windows.

author: Unknown Chinese-speaking operators
target: Low-cost, unofficial Android TV set-top boxes, tablets, and streaming devices
description: The Kimwolf Android botnet has infected over 2 million devices, primarily low-cost Android TV boxes. It monetizes through massive DDoS attacks (peaking at 30 Tbps), unauthorized application installations, and the sale of residential proxy bandwidth.
country: VN BR IN SA US PH AR CN Other Countries

author: Crimson Collective
description: Crimson Collective claims to have breached US fiber provider Brightspeed, allegedly exfiltrating personal data for over one million customers. The stolen data includes names, addresses, emails, and payment details. Brightspeed is investigating the claims, though the hackers shared proof of the breach with dark web monitoring experts.

author: Zestix (a.k.a. Sentap)
target: Approximately 50 global enterprises in the mining, manufacturing, construction, transportation, real estate, professional/scientific, public administration, and human health sectors
description: Researchers at Hudson Rock revealed that "Zestix" (alias "Sentap") compromised over 50 global companies by exploiting credentials harvested from infostealer malware. The attacker accessed cloud storage portals like ShareFile and Nextcloud that lacked multi-factor authentication, exfiltrating sensitive data including aircraft manuals, defense blueprints, and medical records for financial gain.
country: US ES TR BR PE CA RO IT AU

author: Unknown
description: A cyberattack forces Higham Lane School in Nuneaton to remain closed after the Christmas holidays. The incident disabled all digital services, including telephones, emails, and servers.

author: Suspected Russian cybercriminals
description: Researchers at Securonix discover "PHALT#BLYX", a campaign carried out by Russian threat actors, targeting European hotels with fake booking cancellations that trick staff into triggering a fake "Blue Screen of Death." This social engineering technique forces victims to run malicious commands, installing the DCRat Trojan to steal passwords and monitor keystrokes.

author: Unknown
target: Multiple orgenizations using Legacy D-Link DSL gateway models (e.g., DSL-2640B, DSL-2740R, DSL-2780B, DSL-526B)
description: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical command injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-0625) in legacy D-Link DSL routers. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution, enabling attackers to hijack DNS settings and control network traffic. Because these devices are end-of-life, no security patches will be released, leaving users permanently at risk.

author: Black Cat
description: CNCERT/CC and ThreatBook discover a campaign where the threat actor Black Cat uses SEO poisoning to push malicious, high-ranking sites to search results.

author: Unknown
description: Gulshan Management Services, a Texas-based gas station and convenience store operator, suffers a ransomware attack impacting over 377,000 individuals.

author: Unknown
target: Organizations with complex email routing and misconfigured spoof protections
description: Researchers at Microsoft discover that attackers are exploiting "direct send" mail flow methods and misconfigured third-party connectors. By sending emails that appear to originate from the victim’s own domain, they deliver AiTM phishing lures to steal credentials and bypass MFA, leveraging trust in internal communications to increase success rates.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Check Point discover the GoBruteforcer botnet targeting crypto and blockchain project databases. Exploiting weak credentials in AI-generated configurations and outdated XAMPP stacks, the malware deploys web shells and wallet-draining tools, specifically targeting TRON and Binance Smart Chain addresses to identify and steal non-zero balances.

author: Unknown (unidentified "malicious cyber actors").
target: Organizations in the U.S. utilizing HPE OneView infrastructure
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-37164, a maximum-severity flaw in HPE OneView to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

author: Unknown (unidentified "malicious cyber actors").
target: Organizations in the U.S. utilizing Microsoft PowerPoint
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2009-0556, a code injection vulnerability in Microsoft Office PowerPoint to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

author: Chinese-speaking threat actors
target: Organizations using VMware ESXi and SonicWall VPN appliances
description: Researchers at Huntress discover Chinese-speaking threat actors exploiting three VMware ESXi zero-days (CVE-2025-22224, CVE-2025-22225, CVE-2025-22226) in December 2025. The attack involved a sophisticated toolkit for VM escapes and hypervisor backdoors, potentially developed over a year before the vulnerabilities were publicly disclosed and patched in March 2025.

author: Zestix (a.k.a. Sentap)
description: Spanish airline Iberia clarifies that a recent data breach report involved a November 2024 incident where the threat actor "Zestix" stole 77 GB of data from its ShareFile portal. The breach, facilitated by infostealer malware, compromised customer contact details and technical aircraft documentation without impacting flight safety.

author: wenmoonx
target: Cryptocurrency developers and users of npm packages; specifically those using Chrome, MetaMask, and API tokens
description: Researchers at Zscaler ThreatLabz discover NodeCordRAT, a novel remote access trojan hidden in Bitcoin-themed npm packages. It fingerprints infected systems (Windows, Linux, macOS), executes shell commands, and exfiltrates sensitive browser data and crypto wallet seed phrases via Discord’s API.

author: APT28 (a.k.a. BlueDelta, Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard, or Fighting Ursa)
target: Turkish Energy and Nuclear Energy Research Agency (TENMAK), a European think tank, military/government entities in North Macedonia, and an IT integrator in Uzbekistan.
description: Researchers at Recorded Future discover APT28 using phishing campaigns to harvest credentials. The group utilized fake Microsoft OWA and Google login pages, leveraging legitimate web services like Webhook.site and InfinityFree to host malicious infrastructure and exfiltrate data, primarily targeting energy, defense, and policy organizations to support Russian intelligence.

author: Salt Typhoon (a.k.a. GhostEmperor or FamousSparrow)
target: U.S. House of Representatives staff (specifically those on the House Select Committee on China, Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and Armed Services committees)
description: Chinese threat actors linked to the "Salt Typhoon" group infiltrated the email systems of U.S. House of Representatives staff. The breach, primarily affecting committees overseeing national security, foreign affairs, and intelligence, highlights persistent vulnerabilities in government communications and ongoing state-backed espionage efforts targeting sensitive legislative planning.

author: Unknown
description: Monroe University (formerly Monroe College) confirms a cyberattack involving unauthorized network access. Between December 9 and 23, 2024, threat actors exfiltrated a massive trove of sensitive documents containing personal, medical, and financial data of over 320,000 individuals, including students and staff, potentially leading to identity theft.

author: Kimsuky (a.k.a. APT43, Black Banshee, Thallium, Velvet Chollima, Emerald Sleet, Springtail, TA427)
target: U.S. organizations including NGOs, think tanks, academic institutions, strategic advisory firms, and government entities
description: The FBI discovers Kimsuky threat actors using malicious QR codes in spearphishing emails targeting U.S. organizations. Victims scanning these codes are redirected to mobile-optimized phishing pages that harvest credentials and session tokens.

author: UAT-7290 (Linked to Red Foxtrot and APT10; a.k.a. CL-STA-0969)
target: Multiple Organizations including critical infrastructure, healthcare, manufacturing, and professional services.
description: Researchers at Cisco Talos discover UAT-7290, a China-linked threat actor targeting telcos since 2022. They use one-day exploits and SSH brute-forcing on edge devices to deploy Linux malware like RushDrop and SilentRaid. The group also builds relay infrastructure for other China-nexus actors to use in separate cyberattacks.

author: Unknown Threat Actor(s)
description: Threat actors steal over $26.4 million in Ethereum from the Truebit platform. The company halts smart contract interactions while investigating with law enforcement.

author: Astaroth (a.k.a. Guildma) operators, also tracked as PINEAPPLE, Water Makara, or STAC3150
target: Individual retail banking customers and financial service users in Brazil
description: Researchers at Acronis discover the "Boto Cor-de-Rosa" campaign. It features a Python-based worm that hijacks WhatsApp Web to message a victim's contacts with malicious ZIP files. Once opened, a VBS script installs the Astaroth trojan to monitor browsing and harvest credentials from banking websites.

author: MuddyWater (a.k.a. Mango Sandstorm, Static Kitten, TA450, UNG0801)
target: Diplomatic, maritime, financial, and telecom entities; also IT, MSPs, and HR firms
description: Researchers at CloudSEK discover an Iranian campaign using spear-phishing emails with malicious Word documents. Victims are tricked into enabling macros that deploy "RustyWater," a Rust-based Trojan. This malware provides asynchronous command-and-control, anti-analysis features, and registry persistence, allowing attackers to expand post-compromise capabilities while maintaining a low profile.

author: Unknown
description: JPMorgan Chase notifies clients of a data breach at the external law firm Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson LLP. The breach potentially exposed sensitive investor data, though the bank's internal systems were not compromised.

author: Unknown
description: Fintech firm Betterment confirms a data breach after attackers exploited a third-party marketing platform to send fraudulent "triple your crypto" scam emails. While the attackers accessed customer contact details—including names and birthdates—Betterment maintains that core systems, login credentials, and investment accounts remain secure and were not directly compromised.

author: Unknown
target: Users and Organizations Utilizing the n8n Workflow Automation Platform
description: Researchers at Endor Labs discover that attackers exploited n8n's trust in community-maintained integrations. By masquerading as Google Ads connectors, malicious npm packages lured users into entering OAuth credentials, which were then decrypted at runtime and exfiltrated to a command-and-control server, bypassing traditional security controls.

author: dk0m
target: Armenian government (specifically the electronic civil litigation and notification systems)
description: Armenian authorities are investigating the alleged sale of 8 million government records on a hacker forum for $2,500. The dataset reportedly includes official notifications from police and judicial bodies. While officials deny a direct email infrastructure breach, they suggest data may have originated from a civil litigation platform.

author: Unknown
description: Betterment, a robo-advisor, discloses a data breach resulting from a social engineering attack on third-party marketing and operations platforms. While customer accounts and credentials remained secure, a threat actor accessed personal information including names and contact details, subsequently sending fraudulent crypto-related scam messages to users.

author: Unknown
description: Respawn Entertainment discovers and confirms an active security incident where a "bad actor" remotely manipulated player inputs mid-match. This allowed the attacker to move characters and activate cheats without the players' consent, leading to the immediate suspension of competitive play to protect game integrity and player safety.

author: Unknown
description: Eurail discloses a significant data breach involving personal, order, and reservation information of customers using Eurail or Interrail passes. The compromise includes identity details and passport information.

author: Unknown
description: Spanish energy giant Endesa suffers a major data breach after a threat actor gained unauthorized access to its commercial platform. The attacker exfiltrated roughly 1.05 terabytes of sensitive data, including customer identification, contact details, DNI numbers, and payment information (IBANs), impacting millions of electricity and gas customers in Spain.

author: Unknown
description: The University of Hawaiʻi reports a ransomware attack where threat actors encrypted servers and exfiltrated sensitive study participant data. Despite discovering the breach in August, officials did not notify the legislature until December or inform affected individuals immediately, choosing instead to pay the ransom to protect the data.

author: Unknown
description: CISA adds a high-severity path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2025-8110) in Gogs, a self-hosted Git service, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Attackers bypass previous security fixes using symbolic links to overwrite sensitive configuration files, achieving remote code execution. Over 700 instances have already been compromised globally.

author: Void Blizzard (a.k.a. UAC-0190 or Laundry Bear)
description: CERT-UA discloses a targeted cyber-espionage campaign against the Ukrainian Armed Forces involving the PLUGGYAPE backdoor. Russia-aligned group UAC-0190 (Void Blizzard) used fake charity-themed social engineering via Signal and WhatsApp to deceive personnel into downloading malicious executables, facilitating remote code execution and long-term surveillance through WebSocket/MQTT protocols.

author: A threat actor using the alias "Sc0rpion"
description: A threat actor using the alias "Sc0rpion" claims to have stolen Target’s source code and developer documentation after breaching its internal GitHub Enterprise and Jira servers. In response, the American retail giant takes its development infrastructure offline to investigate. Some stolen data was leaked on a hacking forum as proof of the intrusion. The day after some employees confirm the breach.

author: Unknown
target: Facebook users and organizations (via copyright infringement lures)
description: Researchers at Trellix discover that attackers are using the Browser-in-the-Browser (BitB) technique to spoof Facebook login pop-ups. By hosting malicious pages on legitimate cloud services like Netlify and Vercel, they bypass security filters to steal credentials and harvest personal data for identity fraud and scam distribution.

author: Unknown
description: South Korean conglomerate Kyowon Group confirms a ransomware attack that compromised 600 of its 800 servers, potentially exposing data for up to 9.6 million accounts. The group shut down systems across its education, travel, and healthcare affiliates to contain the breach while investigating the extent of the stolen information.

author: Unknown
description: Central Maine Healthcare (CMH) reports a data breach affecting 145,381 patients and employees. Between March and June 2025, unauthorized actors accessed the network, stealing sensitive personal information, including Social Security numbers and medical treatment details. CMH finalized its investigation in November 2025, offering credit monitoring to those impacted.

author: SHADOW#REACTOR
description: Securonix researchers identify the "SHADOW#REACTOR" campaign, which uses a multi-stage attack chain to deploy the Remcos RAT. The process involves obfuscated VBScript and PowerShell to download fragmented payloads, eventually utilizing MSBuild.exe to execute the malware in memory, allowing persistent remote access and data theft while evading traditional security detection.

author: jorjortan142
target: Users of the MEXC cryptocurrency exchange
description: Researchers at Socket discover a malicious Chrome extension masquerading as a trading tool. It injects scripts into authenticated MEXC sessions to generate API keys with withdrawal rights, visually masks the permissions to deceive users, and transmits the credentials to a Telegram bot controlled by the attacker.

author: Unknown
description: The Belgian hospital AZ Monica suffers a cyberattack, forcing it to shut down all servers across its Antwerp and Deurne campuses. The incident disrupts digital medical records, leading to the cancellation of non-urgent procedures and the transfer of critical patients to other regional medical facilities.

author: Unknown
target: Users and organizations running vulnerable versions of Microsoft Windows
description: Microsoft Patch Tuesday security updates for January 2026 fixes CVE-2026-20805, a Windows Desktop Window Manager vulnerability, actively exploited in attacks in the wild. Shortly after the vulnerability is added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerability catalog.

author: Unknown Magecart-style threat actors
target: Customers of major payment networks (Mastercard, Visa, American Express, etc.) and WordPress-based e-commerce shops
description: Researchers at Silent Push discover a campaign where actors inject malicious JavaScript (like "recorder.js") into web shops. The script identifies administrative sessions to hide itself and replaces legitimate Stripe payment fields with fraudulent forms to capture sensitive data, including credit card numbers and shipping addresses, before exfiltrating them.

author: Russian security services (specifically linked to "Russian sabotage" by Polish officials)
target: Poland's energy infrastructure (specifically communications between renewable energy sources and distribution operators)
description: Poland thwars a massive Russian-linked cyberattack targeting its energy grid. Attackers attempted to disrupt communications between renewable energy installations and distribution operators to cause a nationwide blackout during a severe cold snap. Polish officials described it as a coordinated sabotage effort that was successfully repelled.

author: Unknown
target: Whitebox Technologies (third-party service provider for the Anchorage Police Department)
description: The Anchorage Police Department takes servers offline following a cyberattack on its service provider, Whitebox Technologies. Although no APD systems were compromised, officials disabled vendor access and removed data as a precaution.

author: Unknown
description: The Victorian Department of Education notifies parents that hackers breached a database containing student names, email addresses, and encrypted passwords. The access occurred via a single school's network. While thousands of current and former students are affected, authorities found no evidence of data being publicly released.

author: Unknown
target: Employees in finance, procurement, supply chain, and administration within the oil, gas, import, and export sectors
description: Researchers at Trellix discover an active campaign exploiting a DLL side-loading flaw in the legitimate ahost.exe utility. Attackers use a malicious libcares-2.dll to execute code, bypassing signature-based defenses to deploy various commodity malware like Agent Tesla, Formbook, and XWorm across multiple global regions.

author: Unknown
target: Over 40,000 WordPress websites using the Modular DS plugin
description: Researchers at Patchstack reveal that a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-23550, CVSS 10.0) in the WordPress "Modular DS" plugin is being actively exploited. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication and gain administrative access by exploiting misconfigured routing, leading to full site compromise.

author: Unknown
description: Canada’s investment regulator, CIRO, confirms that a sophisticated attack compromised the personal data of 750,000 investors. Following a 9,000-hour forensic investigation, the regulator revealed that sensitive information, including Social Insurance Numbers and account statements, was stolen, though login credentials remained secure.

author: UAT-8837
target: High-value critical infrastructure organizations in North America
description: Researchers at Cisco Talos reveal that the Chinese-linked actor UAT-8837 breached critical infrastructure by exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities (e.g., CVE-2025-53690 in SiteCore) and stolen credentials. They utilized tools such as Earthworm for internal endpoint exposure and exfiltrated security data to facilitate persistent, long-term access to victim networks.

author: ShinyHunters (a.k.a. UNC6395 by Google/Mandiant)
description: Grubhub confirms a security breach after threat actors accessed systems and stole data, including Zendesk information used for customer support. While financial details weren't compromised, the company is reportedly facing extortion. The attack is linked to a broader campaign involving stolen credentials from previous breaches at platforms like Salesloft and Drift.

author: "GhostPoster"
target: General internet users and e-commerce platform visitors
description: Researchers at LayerX discover an evolved GhostPoster variant, using "steganography" to hide malicious payloads within extension icons and background scripts. The malware remains dormant to evade detection before hijacking browser traffic for financial gain through affiliate fraud and unauthorized ad injection across various web browsers.

author: "databycloud1104" and "Software Access"
target: Enterprise users of HR and ERP platforms (specifically Workday, NetSuite, and SAP SuccessFactors)
description: Researchers at Socket discover five malicious Chrome extensions masquerading as enterprise productivity tools. These extensions exfiltrated session cookies every 60 seconds, blocked administrative security pages to hinder incident response, and performed bidirectional cookie injection to bypass multi-factor authentication, allowing immediate and persistent account takeover of high-value corporate platforms.

author: Unspecified threat actors
target: Organizations using Fortinet FortiSIEM versions 6.7 through 7.5
description: Researchers at Defused reveal that threat actors are exploiting a critical command injection vulnerability (CVE-2025-64155) in Fortinet FortiSIEM.

date_discovered_raw: Early January 2026 (following the January 3, 2026, geopolitical events mentioned as lures)
author: Mustang Panda (a.k.a Earth Pret, HoneyMyte, and Twill Typhoon)
description: Researchers at Acronis discover a Mustang Panda campaign targeting U.S. policy entities. Using Venezuela-themed spear-phishing, attackers delivered the LOTUSLITE backdoor through ZIP archives. The malware uses DLL side-loading to execute, providing attackers with remote shell access, file management capabilities, and persistent control over infected systems for data exfiltration.
