author: Unknown
description: Gulshan Management Services discloses a ransomware attack.

author: SafePay
description: Ingram Micro confirms that a July 2025 ransomware attack compromised the personal data of over 42,000 individuals, including employees and job applicants. Sensitive information such as Social Security numbers and passport details was stolen by the SafePay group, which previously claimed to have exfiltrated 3.5 terabytes of internal data.

author: KongTuke (a.k.a. 404 TDS, Chaya_002, LandUpdate808, TAG-124)
target: Corporate environments and individual web users
description: Researchers at Huntress discover the "CrashFix" campaign where a fake ad-blocker extension (NexShield) intentionally crashes the user's browser. It then displays a fake security warning to lure users into running malicious PowerShell commands, which ultimately deploy the previously undocumented ModeloRAT remote access trojan on corporate machines.

author: Unknown
target: High-profile Gmail and WhatsApp users, including activists, journalists, and academics
description: A sophisticated Iranian-linked phishing campaign targets high-profile individuals in the Middle East. Attackers impersonated tech support via WhatsApp to lure victims to fake Gmail login pages, aiming to steal credentials, hijack accounts, and perform surveillance through location tracking, photo theft, and audio recordings.
country: Multiple countries in Middle East and not only, including: IL LB US

author: Unknown
target: Canonical Snap Store users and Linux developers
description: Threat actors are monitoring the Snap Store for publishers using expired email domains. By re-registering these domains, hackers gain account recovery access, allowing them to hijack established software packages and replace legitimate code with malware, which is then automatically distributed to unsuspecting Linux users.

author: Qilin (a.k.a. Agenda)
target: A Fortune 100 company in the financial sector
description: Researchers at Resecurity discover PDFSider, a sophisticated backdoor deployed via spear-phishing and DLL side-loading. It evades security tools by executing primarily in memory, performing anti-VM checks, and using encrypted DNS traffic for command-and-control communication, facilitating long-term persistence and remote command execution within high-value enterprise networks.

author: Unknown
target: Several Iranian state television channels tramsmitted via the Badr satellite
description: Several Iranian state television channels are briefly hijacked, interrupting regular programming to air protest footage and messages from an exiled opposition figure, according to multiple media reports.

author: Unknown (associated with the handle "BigBlack" or "mrbigblacktheme" in extension names).
target: Software developers and organizations using Visual Studio Code
description: Researchers at Trend Micro reveal that attackers are weaponizing malicious Visual Studio Code extensions to deploy "Evelyn Stealer," a multi-stage infostealer. The malware targets developers to harvest credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and system data. By compromising developer environments, threat actors gain high-privileged entry points into broader corporate networks and sensitive cloud infrastructures.

author: Nomad Leopard
target: Afghan government ministries and administrative offices
description: Researchers at Seqrite discover "Nomad Leopard", a phishing campaign targeting Afghan government employees using fake official correspondence from the prime minister's office. The attack utilizes decoy documents signed by officials to lure victims into downloading "FalseCub" malware from GitHub, designed for data exfiltration and extensive institutional espionage.

author: US
target: Venezuelan National Power Grid (CORPOELEC) and government communications.
description: Reports link cyberattacks to the capture of Nicolás Maduro and a Venezuelan nationwide blackout. Operations targeted electrical infrastructure and military communications to facilitate "Operation Libertad." Experts suggest high-level coordination between physical tactical movements and cyber-disruption of the SCADA systems controlling the Guri Dam power plant.

author: Unnamed "malicious actor" (resembles tactics of groups like CryptoChameleon/UNC5356)
description: LastPass warns of a phishing campaign impersonating maintenance alerts to steal master passwords. Attackers send emails urging users to back up vaults within 24 hours via a malicious link. The scam creates false urgency to harvest credentials, potentially compromising all passwords stored within the victim's vault.

author: Unknown (likely opportunistic cybercriminals or state-sponsored groups using DLL sideloading tactics similar to Mustang Panda or North Korean actors)
target: High-value individuals, business executives, and IT administrators
description: Researchers at ReliaQuest discover a campaign where attackers deliver weaponized WinRAR archives via LinkedIn DMs. The attack leverages DLL sideloading with a legitimate open-source PDF reader and Python scripts to bypass traditional security monitoring and establish a persistent backdoor for remote access and data theft on corporate systems.

date_discovered_raw: Since December 2025 with new interactions in January 2026
author: North Korean threat actors (linked to "Contagious Interview" or "PurpleBravo" clusters; a.k.a. Famous Chollima, UNC5342, and DEV#POPPER).
target: Software developers and engineering teams, specifically in the cryptocurrency, blockchain, and fintech sectors.
description: Researchers at JAMF reveal that North Korea-linked threat actors are targeting software developers by using malicious Visual Studio Code projects. Part of the "Contagious Interview" campaign, these attacks lure victims with fake job assessments, tricking them into cloning repositories that execute malicious JavaScript to deliver backdoors and establish remote code execution.

author: Unknown
target: Users in Russia (specifically targeting corporate/business functions like accounting)
description: Researchers from Fortinet discover a multi-stage phishing campaign targeting Russian users with Amnesia RAT and ransomware. Attackers use business-themed decoys and malicious LNK files to execute obfuscated scripts. The infection chain disables Microsoft Defender, exfiltrates data via Telegram, and hijacks file associations to extort victims, ultimately achieving full system compromise silently.

author: Unknown
target: Fortune 500 companies and security vendors (including Cloudflare, F5, and Palo Alto Networks).
description: Researchers at Pentera reveal that threat actors are exploiting misconfigured, intentionally vulnerable security testing applications (like DVWA and OWASP Juice Shop) to breach Fortune 500 cloud environments. These exposures allow attackers to steal credentials, deploy cryptocurrency miners, and plant webshells.

author: Unknown
target: Fortinet FortiGate firewall users with FortiCloud SSO enabled
description: Attackers are exploiting a patch bypass for a critical FortiGate authentication vulnerability (CVE-2025-59718). Despite being updated, admins report unauthorized logins, admin account creation, and potential configuration theft. Arctic Wolf confirms the exploitation.

author: "daghetiaw"
description: PcComponentes denies claims of a 16-million customer data breach, asserting internal systems remain secure. However, it confirmed a credential stuffing attack where hackers used passwords stolen from other breaches to access a small number of accounts. The company has since mandated two-factor authentication and reset user sessions. The customer data breach come probably from an Infostealer infection dating back to 2020.

author: Unknown threat actor (Malware family: Android.Phantom)
description: Researchers at Doctor Web discover the Android.Phantom trojan, which employs TensorFlow.js machine learning to automate ad-fraud. By taking screenshots of a hidden virtual screen, the malware visually identifies and interacts with dynamic ads. It spreads through modified popular apps and games on Xiaomi’s GetApps, Telegram, and Discord, mimicking authentic user behavior.

author: Unknown threat actors
target: Cisco Unified Communications products (including Unified CM, Unified CM SME, IM & Presence, Unity Connection, and Webex Calling).
description: Cisco patches a critical remote code execution (RCE) zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-20045) in its Unified Communications and Webex Calling products. Actively exploited in the wild, the flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute commands with root privileges via crafted HTTP requests, potentially compromising enterprise calling and messaging infrastructure. The day after the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds the flow to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

author: Unknown
description: Security researchers observe threat actors exploiting the Zendesk "Requestor" field. By submitting tickets with a target's email as the "requestor," attackers forced Zendesk to send legitimate-looking but malicious notifications, effectively turning corporate helpdesks into spam relays that bypass traditional email security filters.

author: PurpleBravo (a.k.a. CL-STA-0240, DeceptiveDevelopment, DEV#POPPER, Famous Chollima, Gwisin Gang, Tenacious Pungsan, UNC5342, Void Dokkaebi, and WaterPlum)
target: Organizations in the artificial intelligence (AI), cryptocurrency, financial services, IT services, marketing, and software development sectors
description: Researchers at Recorded Future identify 3,136 individual IP addresses concentrated in South Asia and North America linked to likely targets of PurpleBravo activity from August 2024 to September 2025 as part of the Contagious Interview campaign.
country: Global (Europe, South Asia, the Middle East, and Central America)

author: Unknown
target: Developers and Linux systems using Python (specifically those seeking the SymPy library)
description: Security researchers at Socket discover a malicious PyPI package, sympy-dev, masquerading as a development version of the popular SymPy library. The package targets Linux systems to deploy an XMRig cryptocurrency miner using sophisticated fileless execution techniques to evade detection, while also serving as a general-purpose loader for further attacks.

author: Unnamed threat actors
target: Corporate employees using Microsoft 365 and Gmail services in the energy sector
description: Researchers at Microsoft identify a multi-stage Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) phishing campaign using deceptive emails and reverse proxies to steal session cookies, granting unauthorized access to corporate accounts for financial fraud and business email compromise.

author: Unknown
description: The Dresden State Art Collections (SKD) suffers a cyberattack forcing its entire IT system offline to prevent data theft. While museums remain open, internal communication and digital services are severely disrupted. Authorities are investigating the extent of the breach, with no current evidence of data exfiltration.

author: Everest
description: Under Armour investigates claims of a data breach after a threat actor leaked a database allegedly containing millions of customer email addresses. While the company confirmed it is looking into the matter, it has not yet verified the authenticity of the leaked data or the specific source.

author: Unknown
target: Organizations using SmarterTools SmarterMail email server
description: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in SmarterTools SmarterMail to hijack administrator accounts. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to reset the system administrator password via a crafted HTTP request. Once accessed, attackers can use built-in features to execute operating system commands and gain full control.

author: ShinyHunters?
description: Okta warns that its customers are being targeted by sophisticated vishing campaigns where attackers impersonate IT personnel to reset multi-factor authentication. By convincing service desk staff to reset MFA for privileged accounts, hackers gain super-admin access, allowing them to impersonate users and bypass security controls across the organization.

author: Unknown
target: Servers and IoT devices running legacy Linux distributions with the telnetd package.
description: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-24061) in the GNU InetUtils telnetd server. The flaw allows remote attackers to gain root access. Security experts warn that thousands of legacy systems remain exposed to this trivial-to-exploit "login as root" vulnerability.

author: Unknown (linked to affiliates of INC Ransomware, also known as Warble)
target: Major food service franchisee operator in Southeast Asia
description: Researchers at Broadcom/Symantec detail "Osiris," a sophisticated ransomware targeting a Southeast Asian food service operator. Distinct from a 2016 Locky variant, it utilizes a "Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver" (BYOVD) attack with the POORTRY driver to disable security software before deploying its hybrid encryption payload and exfiltrating data.

author: Unknown
target: Users of Microsoft Outlook, Yahoo!, and AOL.com
description: Researchers at KnowBe4 discover a campaign where attackers use fake Greenvelope invitations to steal credentials. They then use these to register for LogMeIn RMM services, deploying a signed executable ("GreenVelopeCard.exe") that installs a persistent backdoor, allowing unrestricted remote access to Windows systems.

author: Unknown
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-68645, a PHP remote file inclusion vulnerability in Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS), to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation in the wild.

author: Unknown
target: Organizations using Versa Concerto SD-WAN orchestrator
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-34026, an authentication bypass in the Versa Concerto SD-WAN orchestrator, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation in the wild.

author: Unknown
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-31125, an improper access control vulnerability in Vite Vitejs, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation in the wild.

author: Unknown
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-54313, an embedded malicious code vulnerability in eslint-config-prettier, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation in the wild.

author: Jordanian security forces/General Intelligence Directorate
target: Activists, journalists, and protesters in Jordan
description: Jordanian authorities allegedly used Cellebrite technology to extract data from the phones of activists and journalists detained for criticizing the government’s stance on the Gaza war.

author: Unknown
target: Software developers using Visual Studio Code
description: Researchers at Koi find malicious AI-themed extensions on the VS Code Marketplace designed to steal sensitive developer data, including credentials and source code. These extensions impersonated popular tools, tricking developers into installing malware that exfiltrates environment variables and authentication tokens to remote servers, highlighting risks in developer ecosystem supply chains.

author: Konni (linked to North Korean state-sponsored activity).
description: Researchers at Check Point reveal that the Konni group is targeting blockchain engineers via LinkedIn, using AI-generated malware disguised as technical coding assessments. By tricking victims into downloading malicious repositories, the attackers deploy a remote access trojan (RAT) to steal sensitive information and credentials from developers in the cryptocurrency and fintech sectors.

author: Unknown
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2024-37079, a Broadcom VMware vCenter Server vulnerability, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation in the wild.

author: ClearFake (associated with "ClickFix" tactics)
target: General internet users and organizations visiting compromised websites
description: Researchers at Blackpoint Cyber discover a campaign where attackers use fake browser "fix" prompts. When clicked, a PowerShell command is copied to the clipboard. Once executed by the user, it leverages the legitimate Microsoft App-V (Application Virtualization) client to fetch and run malicious scripts that install information-stealing malware.

author: Suspected threat actors from China
description: Researchers from eSentire identify a campaign targeting Indian users with a multi-stage backdoor via phishing emails impersonating the Income Tax Department. The attack deploys Blackmoon malware and a repurposed enterprise tool, SyncFuture TSM, to establish persistent access for continuous monitoring and data exfiltration under a suspected cyberespionage framework.

author: Unknown
target: Users of Microsoft Office and Microsoft 365
description: Microsoft releases emergency out-of-band updates to patch a high-severity Office zero-day (CVE-2026-21509) exploited in targeted attacks. The vulnerability allows attackers to bypass OLE security mitigations by tricking users into opening malicious files. While Office 2021+ received automatic service-side fixes, older versions require manual updates or registry workarounds.

author: ShinyHunters (a.k.a. UNC6040, SLSH, Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters)
description: Threat actors have stolen the personal and contact information belonging to over 29.8 million SoundCloud user accounts after breaching the audio streaming platform's systems.

author: World Leaks
description: Nike is investigating a data breach after the World Leaks extortion group leaked stolen files on their dark web site. The gang claims to have breached Nike’s network and exfiltrated sensitive data, including internal documents, as the company works to determine the full scope and impact of the incident.

author: Unknown
target: Asian government entities and private organizations
description: Researchers at Trend Micro discover SHADOW-EARTH-045, a campaign primarily targeting Asian government entities and private organizations, injecting PeckBirdy links into government websites, likely to deliver scripts for credential harvesting on the website.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Trend Micro discover SHADOW-VOID-044, a campaign targeting Chinese gambling websites with the PeckBirdy JScript-based command-and-control (C2) framework.

author: Possible subgroup of APT36
description: Researchers at Zscaler identify a cyberespionage campaign targeting the Indian government. Attackers used Go-based malware, including GoGitter and GitShellPad, to exfiltrate sensitive data. The campaign utilized GitHub for command-and-control, leveraging phishing lures disguised as official government communications to compromise systems and maintain long-term persistence within high-value networks.

author: Unknown ("Hostile foreign state")
description: Russian security firm Delta confirms a major cyberattack, likely from a "hostile foreign state," which crippled its car and home alarm systems across Russia. While the company denied any data theft, the attackers claimed to have exfiltrated customer databases.

author: ShinyHunters (a.k.a. UNC6040, SLSH, Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters)
description: Crunchbase confirmed a January 2026 data breach after the ShinyHunters hacking group leaked 400MB of stolen data, including over two million records. Part of a campaign targeting multiple tech firms via vishing, the incident involved exfiltrating sensitive corporate documents and PII without disrupting business operations.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at LayerX discover a coordinated campaign of sixteen malicious browser extensions masquerading as legitimate ChatGPT productivity tools. These extensions intercept session authentication tokens, enabling attackers to impersonate users and access private conversations, data, and code.

author: Unknown
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2018-14634, an integer overflow vulnerability in the Linux kernel to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation in the wild.

date_occurred_raw: Ongoing (noted intensification in late 2025 and January 2026)
author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Flare discover a surge in automated attacks where scripts scan for MongoDB instances lacking password protection. Once found, the script exports the data, deletes the original database, and creates a new one containing a ransom note demanding Bitcoin for data recovery.

author: Multiple threat actors, both state-sponsored and financially motivated, including UNC4895 (RomCom/CIGAR), APT44 (FROZENBARENTS), TEMP.Armageddon (CARPATHIAN), Turla (SUMMIT), China-linked actors
description: Researchers from Google Threat Intelligence Group reveal that multiple threat actors, both state-sponsored and financially motivated, are exploiting the CVE-2025-8088 high-severity vulnerability in WinRAR for initial access and to deliver various malicious payloads.

author: HoneyMyte (a.k.a. Mustang Panda or Bronze President)
target: Government entities and organizations in Southeast Asia (Myanmar, Malaysia), Mongolia, Pakistan, and Russia
description: Researchers at Kaspersky analyze an updated campaign by the HoneyMyte APT group (Mustang Panda), featuring enhancements to the CoolClient backdoor. The malware now includes clipboard monitoring, HTTP proxy credential sniffing, and browser login stealers. Targeting Southeast Asia, Russia, and Mongolia, the group utilizes DLL sideloading to maintain persistent espionage.

author: Unknown
target: Fortinet customers using FortiCloud Single Sign-On (SSO).
description: Fortinet temporarily blocks access to FortiCloud SSO to mitigate CVE-2026-24858, a zero-day vulnerability being exploited in the wild. The flaw allows attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to cloud management consoles. The day after the company releases a security patch.

author: Unknown
target: Software developers using Visual Studio Code
description: Researchers from Aikido Security discover a malicious Visual Studio Code extension named "Moltbot," masquerading as an AI coding assistant, stealing sensitive credentials and environment variables from developers. The extension used typo-squatting to mimic the legitimate "Molt" tool, exfiltrating data to a remote server while providing minimal functional AI features to avoid suspicion.

author: 10Xprofit
target: Online retail shoppers (Amazon, AliExpress, Walmart, Shein) and ChatGPT users
description: Researchers at Socket uncover dozens of malicious Chrome extensions, including clusters like "10Xprofit" and "ChatGPT Mods," that hijack affiliate links and steal authentication tokens. These tools impersonate legitimate utilities to exfiltrate session data and redirect e-commerce commissions, compromising millions of users across retail platforms and AI services like ChatGPT.

author: ShinyHunters (a.k.a. UNC6040, SLSH, Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters)
description: ShinyHunters leaks a database containing approximately 5.1 million Panera Bread records, including customer and employee personal information. This 2026 breach, reportedly stemming from a failed ransom negotiation, exposed names, emails, and phone numbers.

author: Hecker (a.k.a. Sakuya, LiveGamer101)
target: Organizations using cloud-hosted Large Language Model (LLM) services and AI infrastructure
description: Researchers from Pilllar Security discover 'Bizarre Bazaar', a malicious campaign actively targeting exposed LLM (Large Language Model) service endpoints to commercialize unauthorized access to AI infrastructure.

author: Unknown
description: Reserchers at Aikido Security discover a typosquatting campaign on PyPI featuring packages like "pyspellchecker-tool." These packages contain malicious code that triggers upon installation, collecting environment variables, AWS credentials, and SSH keys, which are then exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server via encoded HTTP requests.

author: TA584
target: Multiple Organizati0ons in Europe, North America and Oceania
description: Researchers at Proofpoint observe the initial access broker tracked as TA584 using the Tsundere Bot alongside XWorm remote access trojan to gain network access that could lead to ransomware attacks.

author: Unknown
description: A cyberattack on Russia’s Vladimir Bread Factory disables internal digital systems, including accounting and document management. While production remained unaffected, the disruption to order processing and delivery logistics caused regional bread shortages, forcing the manufacturer to revert to manual operations and round-the-clock shifts to maintain food supply chains.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Bitdefender uncover an Android malware campaign leveraging Hugging Face to host a Remote Access Trojan (RAT). Attackers disguise malicious APKs as legitimate tools, utilizing the platform’s infrastructure for command-and-control. The malware exfiltrates sensitive data, intercepts communications, and monitors user activity while evading traditional security detection.

author: Unknown
target: Organizations using Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM), formerly MobileIron Core.
description: Ivanti warns that CVE-2026-1281 and CVE-2026-1340, two zero-day vulnerabilities in its Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM) are being actively exploited. The flaws, a path traversal and a command injection, allow unauthenticated attackers to access sensitive data and execute arbitrary commands on compromised servers, prompting urgent patch recommendations for all affected organizations.

author: ShinyHunters (a.k.a. UNC6040, SLSH, Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters)
description: Match Group confirms a data breach affecting Tinder, Hinge, OkCupid, and Match.com users. Attackers accessed a customer support database containing account information, email addresses, and partial payment details. While passwords and full credit card numbers remained secure, the company is notifying millions of users about potential phishing risks.

author: State-sponsored threat actors
description: Marquis Software Solutions, a Texas-based financial services provider, is blaming a ransomware attack that impacted its systems and affected dozens of U.S. banks and credit unions in August 2025 on a security breach reported by SonicWall a month later.

author: Aisuru/Kimwolf botnet
target: Multiple companies, most of them in the telecommunications sector
description: The Aisuru/Kimwolf botnet launched a new massive distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack that peaked at 31.4 Tbps and 200 million requests per second, setting a new record.

author: Unknown
description: Morphisec reports a critical supply chain compromise in MicroWorld's eScan antivirus product. Malicious updates distributed via legitimate infrastructure delivered multi-stage malware that disables security features and blocks updates.

author: UAT-8099 (associated with China; overlaps with WEBJACK campaign activity)
target: Vulnerable Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS) servers
description: Researchers at Cisco Talos discover UAT-8099 leveraging web shells to deploy the GotoHTTP remote access tool and BadIIS malware. The actor focuses on regional SEO fraud in Southeast Asia, employing sophisticated persistence tools like Sharp4RemoveLog and OpenArk64 to evade security while manipulating search traffic and stealing credentials from high-value targets.

author: ShinyHunters (a.k.a. UNC6040, SLSH, Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters)
description: The threat actor ShinyHunters claims a 30GB data breach of Bumble, allegedly stolen from Google Drive and Slack. Bumble confirmed a contractor account was compromised via a phishing attack but stated user profiles and chats were unaffected. The incident appears to be part of a broader social engineering campaign targeting cloud credentials.

author: RedKitten (suspected Iranian state-sponsored group)
target: Iranian protesters, activists, and human rights organizations
description: Researchers at HarfangLab identified "RedKitten," an AI-accelerated campaign targeting Iranian protesters. Attackers use AI-generated personas and deepfake videos on social media to build trust before deploying modular Python malware via "secure" communication tools. This sophisticated operation highlights the evolving role of generative AI in high-tempo, state-sponsored cyberespionage and surveillance.

author: LockBit
description: The threat actors who attacked OLV Pulhof, a high school in Antwerp, Belgium, are now attempting to extort the parents of individual students after the school refused to pay a ransom.

author: Unknown
target: General consumers and users of cloud storage services (Google One, iCloud, etc.)
description: A massive phishing campaign is flooding inboxes with fake cloud storage renewal notices. Disguised as invoices from services like Google One or iCloud, these emails use urgency and professional branding to trick victims into providing credit card details and personal information on fraudulent payment pages.
country: Global (primarily targeting US and EU users)

author: Glassworm (or actors utilizing the Glassworm loader)
target: Developers using Visual Studio Code and the Open VSX Registry
description: Researchers at Socket discover a malicious "Glassworm" loader targeting VS Code developers via a hijacked Open VSX account. The malware, hidden in an update for the "C# Tools" extension, executes encrypted payloads on Windows systems, demonstrating the severe risks associated with supply chain attacks on developer tooling ecosystems.

author: Author
description: Description

author: Unknown
target: Cryptocurrency holders and users of decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms
description: OpenSourceMalware discovers ClawdBot, a Python info-stealer targeting digital assets. The malware scans for wallet extensions, browser-stored passwords, and session tokens. It employs obfuscation to evade detection and communicates with a Telegram bot to upload stolen archives containing private keys and login credentials from victim machines.

author: UAC-0001 (APT28 a.k.a. Fancy Bear and Sofacy)
description: The Ukraine’s Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) reveals that threat actors from UAC-0001 (APT28)are exploiting CVE-2026-21509, a recently patched vulnerability in multiple versions of Microsoft Office.

author: Unnamed threat actor (Campaign tracked as ClawHavoc
target: Users of the OpenClaw AI assistant
description: Researchers at Koi Security discover 341 malicious skills on ClawHub, a repository for the OpenClaw AI agent. The "ClawHavoc" campaign uses social engineering to trick users into installing malware via fake prerequisites. These tools exfiltrated sensitive data, including browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and SSH keys, from Windows and macOS systems.

author: Unknown
description: Canada Computers & Electronics says a data breach has leaked information about some of its customers.

author: UAC-0001 (APT28 a.k.a. Fancy Bear and Sofacy)
target: Countries in the Central and Eastern European region.
description: Researchers at Zscaler ThreatLabz identify a new campaign in-the-wild, tracked as Operation Neusploit, exploiting exploit CVE-2026-21509, and targeting countries in the Central and Eastern European region.

author: Unknown
target: Organizations using Citrix ADC Gateway and Netscaler Gateway infrastructure
description: Researchers at GreyNoise discover a coordinated campaign targeting Citrix NetScaler systems. Attackers utilized 63,000+ residential proxies to bypass IP-based filters, focusing on identifying login panels and specific software versions. This massive reconnaissance effort indicates deliberate infrastructure mapping for future exploitation rather than opportunistic scanning across global corporate and government networks.

author: Unknown
description: Step Finance reports a $40 million cryptocurrency theft resulting from the compromise of executive devices. Attackers gained access to private keys and multi-signature wallets, draining assets from the Solana-based platform. The company is currently working with law enforcement and security firms to track the stolen funds.

author: Pro-Russian threat actor called Femwar02
target: University of Rome (Università degli Studi di Roma "La Sapienza")
description: Sapienza University of Rome suffers a massive cyberattack, forcing its digital services and official website offline. The university disconnected systems to contain the breach, affecting students and staff access to administrative portals.

author: Lotus Blossom
description: The maintainer of Notepad++ reveals that state-sponsored attackers hijacked the utility's update mechanism to redirect update traffic to malicious servers instead. The attack involved an infrastructure-level compromise that allowed malicious actors to intercept and redirect update traffic destined for notepad-plus-plus.org. The attack is attributed to the Chinese group Lotus Blossom.

author: Multiple threat actors
description: Researches at Microsoft observe macOS targeted infostealer campaigns using social engineering techniques—including ClickFix-style prompts and malicious DMG installers—to deploy macOS-specific infostealers such as DigitStealer, MacSync, and Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS).

author: Unknown
description: A weekend cyberattack on the Uffizi Gallery in Florence disrupts administrative servers and staff email systems but left ticketing, surveillance and visitor services operational, allowing the museum to remain open to the public.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at GreyNoise reveal that, two months after the React2Shell CVE-2025-55182 vulnerability was disclosed, 2025, exploitation activity has consolidated significantly with two IP addresses accounting for 56% of all observed exploitation attempts, down from 1,083 unique sources.

author: Unknown
target: Global corporate employees and IT administrators
description: Researchers at Forcepoint detail a sophisticated phishing campaign exploiting Dropbox’s legitimate infrastructure to host malicious PDFs. By using trusted cloud storage, attackers bypass email filters to deliver credential-stealing links.

author: Unknown
target: Users of Metro Systems Metro4 software
description: Researchers at VulnCheck report that CVE-2025-11953 (a.k.a Metro4Shell), a critical command injection vulnerability in Metro Systems Metro4 software, is being exploited in the wild. Attackers can execute arbitrary code on vulnerable servers, compromising warehouse management and retail operations. Organizations are urged to patch immediately to prevent full system takeover.
country: Global (specifically regions where Metro AG operates, such as DE, RO, PL)

author: Everest
description: Iron Mountain confirms a breach claimed by the Everest extortion gang was limited to marketing materials. Attackers used a compromised credential to access a single folder on a file-sharing server. No customer data was exposed, and no ransomware was involved, leaving core systems and sensitive records unaffected.

author: Unknown
target: Organizations using SolarWinds Web Help Desk
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-40551, a critical SolarWinds Web Help Desk vulnerability, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation in the wild.

author: ‘GordonFreeman’
target: Spain’s Ministry of Science, Innovation, and Universities (Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades)
description: Spain's Ministry of Science (Ministerio de Ciencia) announces a partial shutdown of its IT systems, affecting several citizen- and company-facing services. A threat actor with the moniker ‘GordonFreeman’ claims an attack on the institution's systems and publishes data samples as proof of the breach.

author: Unknown
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2021-39935, a five-year-old GitLab server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation in the wild.

author: Unknown
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2019-19006 Sangoma FreePBX Improper Authentication Vulnerability, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation in the wild.

author: Unknown
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-64328 Sangoma FreePBX OS Command Injection Vulnerability , to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation in the wild.

author: Warlock
description: SmarterTools confirms that the Warlock ransomware gang breached its network after compromising an email system, but it did not impact business applications or account data.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Sysdig disclose the details of an AI-assisted cloud intrusion that escalated from initial access to full administrator privileges in just eight minutes, leveraging LLMs to analyze misconfigurations and automate exploitation.

author: Vect
target: Organizations in Brazil and South Africa
description: Researchers at Red Piranha discover Vect, a new ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group which has already victimized organizations in Brazil and South Africa.

author: Amaranth-Dragon (nexus of APT-41)
target: Governments and law enforcement agencies in Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, Cambodia, Laos, and the Philippines.
description: Researchers at Check Point discover Amaranth-Dragon, a threat actor linked to APT41 state-sponsored Chinese operations, exploiting the CVE-2025-8088 vulnerability in WinRAR in espionage attacks on government and law enforcement agencies.
country: SG TH ID KH LA PH

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Huntress discover threat actors using a vulnerable, signed EnCase Forensic driver to perform a "Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver" (BYOVD) attack. This allows the attacker to execute malicious code in kernel mode, specifically designed to terminate security processes and bypass Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirms that ransomware gangs have begun exploiting CVE-2025-22225, a high-severity VMware ESXi sandbox escape vulnerability that was used in zero-day attacks since at least February 2024.

author: Unnamed threat actors
target: Web servers using Nginx and organizations with public-facing web infrastructure
description: Researchers at Datadog Security Labs detail a sophisticated attack where adversaries modify Nginx configurations to hijack web traffic. By injecting malicious directives, attackers can intercept cleartext credentials, exfiltrate sensitive data, and redirect users to malicious domains, all while maintaining stealth within legitimate infrastructure by bypassing traditional endpoint detection.

author: Unknown
description: Substack notifies users of a data breach after an unauthorized actor accessed an internal system. The incident compromised names, email addresses, and hashed passwords of some subscribers. Substack stated that payment information remained secure, though they urged affected users to change their passwords as a precaution.

author: Qilin (a.k.a. Agenda)
description: Romanian oil pipeline operator Conpet disclosed a cyberattack claimed by the Qilin ransomware gang. The company shut down some systems to contain the breach, though transport operations allegedly remain unaffected. Qilin claimed the theft of over 30GB of data, including financial records and employee information, threatening its release.

author: WantToCry
description: Researchers at Sophos discover that ransomware operators are hosting and delivering malicious payloads at scale by abusing virtual machines (VMs) provisioned by ISPsystem, a legitimate virtual infrastructure management provider.

author: Infy (a.k.a. Prince of Persia)
target: Undisclosed Organizations in India and Germany
description: Unnamed threat actor (Campaign tracked as ClawHavoc)

author: U.S.
target: Separate military system connected to the nuclear sites at Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan
description: According to several U.S. officials, the U.S. military disrupted Iranian air missile defense systems as part of a coordinated operation to destroy the country’s nuclear program, during 2025 strikes

author: NoName057(16)
target: Italian diplomatic missions abroad and sites linked to the upcoming Winter Olympics
description: Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani reveals that Italy thwarted a series of cyberattacks of “Russian origin” targeting diplomatic missions abroad and sites linked to the upcoming Winter Olympics. The attempted attacks hit multiple foreign ministry offices “starting with Washington,” according to Tajani, as well as facilities connected to the 2026 Winter Games, including hotels in the Alpine resort of Cortina d'Ampezzo. The pro-Russian hacker group NoName057(16) claimed responsibility, describing the campaign as retaliation for Italy’s support for Ukraine.

author: UAC-0001 (APT28 a.k.a. Fancy Bear and Sofacy)
description: Researchers at Trellix said they observed broader APT28 activity targeting maritime, transportation and diplomatic entities in countries including Poland, Slovenia, Turkey, Greece and the United Arab Emirates, Exploiting CVE-2026-21509.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Silent Push identif7 more than 10,000 unique infected IP addresses part of the SystemBC botnet.
country: US DE FR SG IN Global

author: ShinyHunters (a.k.a. UNC6040, SLSH, Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters)
description: The ShinyHunters threat actor claims responsibility for last year’s data breaches at the University of Pennsylvania (UPenn) and publishes what it claims are more than 1 million records from the university on the group’s dedicated leak site, which the gang uses to extort its victims.

author: ShinyHunters (a.k.a. UNC6040, SLSH, Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters)
description: The ShinyHunters threat actor claims responsibility for last year’s data breaches at the Harvard University and publishes what it claims are more than 1 million records from the university on the group’s dedicated leak site, which the gang uses to extort its victims.

author: Unknown
target: Organizations using Zendesk and their IT/Security administrators
description: A massive spam wave is hitting Zendesk users, flooding them with thousands of "activate your account" emails. Attackers exploit Zendesk's signup process to bypass spam filters, aiming to bury important security alerts or overwhelm IT support systems.

author: Unnamed ransomware actors
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) is warning that ransomware actors are exploiting CVE-2026-24423, a critical vulnerability in SmarterMail that allows remote code execution without authentication.

In the same day cybersecurity agencies from the Five Eyes intelligence alliance warn that “an advanced threat actor” is actively exploiting CVE-2026-20127 and CVE-2022-20775, pressing organizations to look for signs their systems may already have been compromised.

author: Unknown
description: More than 3 million of people across the U.S. had sensitive information leaked as a result of a 2024 data breach impacting healthcare technology company TriZetto Provider Solutions.

author: 'Indra'
description: DIY store chain ManoMano notifies customers of a data breach that was caused by threat actors compromising a third-party service provider and impacting 37.8 million user accounts.

author: Unknown (impersonating Stripe developers)
target: Developers and organizations using Stripe for payment processing
description: Researchers at ReversingLabs uncover a malicious NuGet package, "Stripe-Official," impersonating the legitimate Stripe SDK. The package contains a sophisticated downloader that executed a malicious script to exfiltrate sensitive system information and developer data.

author: Network of ChatGPT accounts linked to the pro-Kremlin media outlet Rybar
description: OpenAI reveal the details of "Operation “Fish Food", where it banned a network of ChatGPT accounts on Telegram and X linked to the pro-Kremlin media outlet Rybar that used artificial intelligence to generate social media content and draft proposals for covert influence operations targeting Africa.

author: Unknown
target: Ten Mexican government bodies and a financial institution
description: A threat actor exploits Anthropic's Claude chatbot to carry out attacks against Mexican government agencies and financial institutions. The threat actor used Claude to find vulnerabilities in government networks, to write scripts to exploit them, and also tasked the chatbot with finding ways to automate data theft

date_occurred_raw: Since at least as early as December 2025
author: UAT-10027
target: Education and healthcare sectors in the U.S
description: Researchers at Cisco Talos identify a campaign deploying "DoHDoor" malware, which uses DNS-over-HTTPS for covert communication. The attack targets various education and healthcare sectors in the U.S to exfiltrate data and maintain persistence, leveraging legitimate cloud services to hide malicious traffic and bypass traditional network defenses.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Microsoft reveal that threat actors are luring unsuspecting users into running trojanized gaming utilities that are distributed via browsers and chat platforms to distribute a remote access trojan (RAT).

author: APT37 (a.k.a. ScarCruft, Ruby Sleet, and Velvet Chollima)
description: Researchers at Zscaler discover Ruby Jumper, a campaign designed to infiltrate air-gapped networks, leveraging USB drives for lateral movement and data exfiltration.

author: Unknown
target: Go developers working in cryptocurrency and blockchain
description: Researchers at Socket identify a malicious Go module targeting cryptocurrency developers. The package exfiltrates system passwords and deploys the Rekoobe backdoor. By mimicking legitimate cryptographic libraries, the attack enables remote command execution and long-term persistence on Linux systems.

author: Famous Chollima
target: Developers generally in the crypto space
description: Socket researchers identify "StegaBin," an additional interaction of the "Contagious Interview" campaign involving 26 malicious npm packages using steganography to hide malicious payloads in Pastebin. This sophisticated method evades traditional detection, allowing the malware to exfiltrate sensitive data from developers' environments while appearing as harmless dependency updates.

author: Cl0p
description: Madison Square Garden confirms being impacted by a data breach stemming from a cybercrime campaign targeting customers of Oracle’s E-Business Suite (EBS) solution.

author: Unknown
description: South Korea’s National Tax Service exposes publicly the mnemonic recovery phrase of a seized cryptocurrency wallet and someone is able to steal $4.4 million in crypto assets.,

author: Unknown
target: Websites operated by Roskomnadzor (Russian communications watchdog) and the Russian Defense Ministry, as well as infrastructure belonging to the Main Radio Frequency Center (GRFC)
description: Russia’s internet regulator (Roskomnadzor) and defense ministry say their servers were hit by a large distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack that briefly disrupted access to several government websites.

author: Unknown
description: A Chrome extension named "QuickLens - Search Screen with Google Lens" is removed from the Chrome Web Store after it was compromised to push malware and attempt to steal crypto from thousands of users.

author: Unknown
description: More than 38 million accounts are affected by an October 2025 data breach at Canadian giant Canadian Tire.

author: US and Israel
target: Critical infrastructure, official news sites, and security communications systems in Iran
description: Cyberattacks conducted by US-Israeli forces caused widespread disruptions in Iran, including to news/propaganda websites (such as IRNA news agency), communications infrastructure used by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), local applications, and digital government services.

description: Researchers at Infoblox discover that threat actors are abusing the special-use ".arpa" domain and IPv6 reverse DNS in phishing campaigns that more easily evade domain reputation checks and email security gateways.

author: 'Department of Peace'
target: Office of Industry Partnership, part of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS)
description: A group of hacktivists calling themselves “Department of Peace” claimed to have hacked the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), leaking allegedly stolen documents online.

author: Unknown
description: Google releases security updates to patch 129 Android security vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-21385, an actively exploited zero-day flaw in a Qualcomm display component.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Microsoft identify a campaign abusing OAuth redirection vulnerabilities in legitimate cloud applications, redirecting users to authenticate to a malicious application.

author: Unknown
description: Threat actors are exploiting CVE-2026-1492, a critical vulnerability in the User Registration & Membership plugin, which is installed on more than 60,000 WordPress sites.

author: SloppyLemming (a.k.a. Outrider Tiger and Fishing Elephant)
target: Government entities and critical infrastructure operators in Pakistan and Bangladesh
description: Researchers at Arctic Wolf tracks a cyber espionage campaign by SloppyLemming (India-nexus) targeting Pakistani and Bangladeshi government and critical infrastructure. The actor used PDF lures and macro-enabled Excel files to deploy BurrowShell and Rust-based malware via DLL sideloading, leveraging Cloudflare Workers for command-and-control infrastructure.

author: Former Black Basta affiliates or actors co-opting their modus operandi
description: Researchers at Huntress discover a sophisticated campaign where attackers used spam and fake tech support calls to trick users into installing a modified Havoc Command and Control (C2) framework. The attack involved social engineering, DLL sideloading, and rapid lateral movement, likely aiming for data exfiltration or ransomware deployment.

author: Dust Specter, suspected Iran-nexus threat actor (linked to TTPs of groups like APT34).
target: Government officials in Iraq, specifically those affiliated with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
description: Researchers at Scaler identify a campaign by "Dust Specter," a suspected Iran-nexus threat actor, targeting Iraqi government officials. The operation used custom .NET malware (SPLITDROP, TWINTASK, TWINTALK, GHOSTFORM) and social engineering lures like fake Webex invites. Evidence suggests the attackers used generative AI to assist in developing their malicious code.

author: Israel
description: Israel hacked into Tehran’s extensive traffic camera network in order to track the bodyguards of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and other top Iranian officials ahead of assassination of the supreme leader.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Resecurity report that Ariomex’s database, one of Iran’s cryptocurrency exchange platforms, suffered a data leak.

author: Unknown
target: Individual Google account users and corporate employees
description: Researchers at Malwarebytes discover a campaign where users are redirected to a fake Google security page. It prompts the installation of a "security update" extension as a PWA (a Progressive Web App, which is actually a Remote Access Trojan. This allows the attacker to hijack the browser, exfiltrate credentials, and bypass multi-factor authentication.

author: Unknown
description: Cloud Imperium Games (CIG), the game company behind Star Citizen and Squadron 42, says attackers breached systems containing some users' personal information in January.

author: FulcrumSec
description: American data analytics company LexisNexis Legal & Professional confirms that threat actors breached its servers and accessed some customer and business information, after a threat actor named FulcrumSec leaks 2GB of files.

author: Anubis
description: The multinational Dutch paint company AkzoNobel confirms that threat actors breached the network of one of its U.S. sites, following a data leak from the Anubis ransomware gang, which claimed to have stolen from AkzoNobel 170 GB of data, almost 170,000 files.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2026-22719, a VMware Aria Operations vulnerability, to its Known Exploited Vulnerability (KEV) catalog.

author: Multiple threat actors including UNC6353 (Russian cyber espionage group) and UNC6691 (Chinese financially-motivated threat actor)
description: Researchers at Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reveal that a previously undocumented set of 23 iOS exploits named “Coruna” has been deployed by multiple threat actors in targeted espionage campaigns and financially motivated attacks. Few days later the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) orders federal agencies to patch the three iOS security flaws.

author: Unknown
description: Password management software provider LastPass warns users of a phishing campaign targeting its users with fake unauthorized account access alerts.

author: Silver Dragon (also linked to APT41)
target: Organizations and government entities in Southeast Asia and Europe.
description: Researchers at Check Point Research identify Silver Dragon, a Chinese-nexus threat actor (likely under APT41), targeting government entities in Southeast Asia and Europe. The group uses GearDoor, a novel backdoor leveraging Google Drive for command-and-control, alongside custom tools for persistence, screen monitoring, and remote access via hijacked services.

author: 'nhattuanbl'
target: Laravel (PHP) developers and web applications utilizing the Packagist repository.
description: Researchers at Socket uncover malicious Packagist packages, including lara-helper and simple-queue, disguised as Laravel utilities. These packages deploy an encrypted Remote Access Trojan (RAT) via Composer, granting attackers full remote control, shell execution, and data exfiltration capabilities on compromised Windows, macOS, and Linux servers.

author: APT28 (a.k.a. Fancy Bear)
description: Researchers at ClearSky identify a Russian campaign targeting Ukraine using two new malware strains: BadPaw, a .NET-based loader, and MeowMeow, a sophisticated backdoor. The attack uses phishing emails with lure documents regarding border crossing appeals to infect victims.

author: 12 different groups, including Keymous+, DieNet, and NoName057(16)
description: Cybersecurity researchers warn of a surge in retaliatory hacktivist activity following the U.S.-Israel coordinated military campaign against Iran, codenamed Epic Fury and Roaring Lion.

author: Suspected Iranian threat actors
target: Israeli civilians and potentially military reservists using the RedAlert emergency application.
description: Researchers at CloudSEK discover an espionage campaign where attackers lure victims into sideloading a weaponized "RedAlert" app via SMS phishing. The malware mimics the official IDF Home Front Command interface to steal SMS, contacts, and GPS data, while using anti-detection techniques to bypass standard Android integrity checks.

author: Unknown
description: Customers of restaurants using the HungerRush point-of-sale (POS) platform say they received emails from a threat actor attempting to extort the company, warning that restaurant and customer data could be exposed if HungerRush fails to respond. HungerRush confirms the breach but denies the attacker's claims.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Huntress discover fake OpenClaw installers hosted in GitHub repositories and promoted by Microsoft Bing’s AI-enhanced search feature instructing users to run commands that deployed information stealers and proxy malware.

author: Unknown
description: Passaic County, one of the largest counties in New Jersey reveals to be dealing with a cyberattack that disrupted the phone lines and IT systems used across government offices.

author: Suspected Iranian threat actors
target: Internet-connected surveillance cameras (specifically Hikvision and Dahua brands) in israel, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, the UAE, Cyprus and Lebanon
description: Researchers at Check Point reveal a surge in attempts to compromise internet-connected surveillance cameras across the Middle East during the ongoing regional conflict, with activity attributed to infrastructure linked to Iranian threat actors.

description: ​Cisco flags two Catalyst SD-WAN Manager security flaws (CVE-2026-20122 and CVE-2026-20128) as actively exploited in the wild, urging administrators to upgrade vulnerable devices.

description: The Wikimedia Foundation suffers a security incident today after a self-propagating JavaScript worm began modifying user scripts and vandalizing Meta-Wiki pages.

author: UAT-9244 (China-nexus APT closely associated with Famous Sparrow and Tropic Trooper)
description: Researchers at Cisco Talos discover a China-linked advanced persistent threat actor tracked as UAT-9244 targeting telecommunication service providers in South America since 2024, compromising Windows, Linux, and network-edge devices.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2023-41974, an Apple iOS and iPadOS use-after-free vulnerability, to its Known Exploited Vulnerability (KEV) catalog.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Microsoft identify a widespread ClickFix social engineering campaign leveraging Windows Terminal as the primary execution mechanism.

author: Seedworm (a.k.a. MuddyWater, Temp Zagros, Static Kitten)
target: Multiple organizations including a U.S. bank, airport, non-profit and the Israeli operations of a U.S. software company were among the targets
description: Researchers at Broadcom/Symantec reveal that the Iranian APT group Seedworm targeted U.S. and Israeli entities with a new backdoor called Dindoor.

author: APT36, a.k.a. Transparent Tribe
target: South Asian regional politics and national security
description: Researchers at Bitdefender reveal that the thret actor APT36 has become the latest hacking group to embrace artificial intelligence (AI)-powered coding tools to strike targets with various implants.

author: Unknown
description: The FBI says that it is investigating “suspicious activities” on an internal system that contains sensitive information related to surveillance operations and investigations.

author: Suspected Russian threat actors
target: Windows users seeking free software tools, performance boosters, or cracked versions of legitimate utilities
description: Researchers at Trend Micro discover the "BoRyptGrab" campaign, where attackers use SEO-optimized GitHub repositories and deceptive pages to distribute information-stealing malware to Windows users. The attack chain delivers multiple payloads, including a reverse SSH backdoor (TunnesshClient), targeting browser data, cryptocurrency wallets, and sensitive system files.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Push Security discover a new variation of the ClickFix social engineering technique called InstallFix, used to convince users into running malicious commands under the pretext of installing legitimate command-line interface (CLI) tools such as the Claude Code CLI.

author: Unknown
description: TriZetto Provider Solutions, a healthcare IT company that develops software and services used by health insurers and healthcare providers discloses a data breach that exposed the sensitive information of over 3.4 million people.

author: Blitz Brigantine (a.k.a. Storm-1811, STAC5777)
target: Employees at financial and healthcare organizations
description: Researchers at BlueVoyant identify a sophisticated social engineering campaign deploying the "A0Backdoor." Attackers impersonate IT support via Microsoft Teams and Quick Assist to gain remote access. Once inside, they use the custom backdoor to exfiltrate sensitive data and establish persistence.

author: CL-UNK-1068 (assessed to be a Chinese threat actor)
target: High-value organizations across South, Southeast and East Asia.
description: Researchers at Palo Alto Networks identify a long-running Chinese threat cluster, CL-UNK-1068, targeting critical sectors in Asia since 2020. The group uses a diverse toolkit, including custom scanners, modified open-source utilities, and DLL side-loading via legitimate Python executables to conduct persistent cyberespionage and data exfiltration.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Cyfirma discover TaxiSpy, a sophisticated Android hybrid (Banking Trojan and RAT) targeting Russian financial users. It captures credentials and OTPs while providing full remote device control via WebSockets and Firebase.

author: Unknown
target: Users of the WorkFlowy desktop application and individuals
description: Researchers at Atos discover a new ClickFix variant using "net use" to map malicious WebDAV drives. Attackers trick users into executing commands via the Win+R shortcut, deploying a trojanized WorkFlowy application.

author: Unknown
target: Multiple organizations using Gladinet CentreStack, SmarterMail or SmarterTools, Solarwinds Web Help Desk
description: Researchers at Huntress discover a threat actor exploiting vulnerabilities, including SolarWinds Web Help Desk, to exfiltrate system data into a free trial Elastic Cloud SIEM instance. The attacker used the SIEM’s legitimate triage tools to manage multiple victims, effectively repurposing professional security infrastructure to organize their own malicious campaign.

author: INC Ransomware
description: Cybersecurity authorities in Oceania warn that the INC ransomware operation has been ripping through healthcare organizations in the region.

author: ShinyHunters
description: Salesforce warns customers that threat actors are targeting websites with misconfigured Experience Cloud platforms that give guest users access to more data than intended. However, the ShinyHunters extortion gang claims to be actively exploiting a new bug to steal data from instances.

author: 'openclaw-ai'
target: Developers and users of AI integration utilities/SDKs, specifically those looking for "OpenClaw."
description: Researchers at Jfrog discover "GhostClaw," a malicious npm package impersonating the AI tool "OpenClaw" to compromise developers. It uses a fake CLI to steal system passwords, exfiltrate credentials, browser data, and crypto wallets, while installing a persistent Remote Access Trojan (RAT) for long-term surveillance and C2 communication.

author: Unknown
target: Individuals and Businesses in the U.S.
description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) warns that criminals are impersonating U.S. officials in phishing attacks targeting businesses and individuals who request city and county planning and zoning permits.

author: Unknown
description: Ericsson Inc., the U.S. subsidiary of Swedish networking and telecommunications giant Ericsson, says threat actors have stolen data belonging to over 15,000 employees and customers after hacking one of its service providers.

author: Russian state threat actors
target: Dignitaries, military personnel and civil servants in the Netherlands
description: The Dutch intelligence and security services MIVD and AIVD reveal that Russian state threat actors are engaged in a large-scale global cyber campaign to gain access to Signal and WhatsApp accounts belonging to dignitaries, military personnel and civil servants.

author: Unknown
description: CISA flags CVE-2026-1603, a high-severity Ivanti Endpoint Manager (EPM) vulnerability as actively exploited in attacks and orders U.S. federal agencies to patch systems within three weeks.

author: UNC4899 a.k.a. Jade Sleet, PUKCHONG, Slow Pisces, and TraderTraitor
description: Researchers at Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reveal that the North Korean threat actor known as UNC4899 is suspected to be behind a sophisticated cloud compromise campaign targeting a cryptocurrency organization in 2025 to steal millions of dollars in cryptocurrency.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2021-22054, a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Omnissa Workspace One UEM (formerly VMware Workspace One UEM), to its Known Exploited Vulnerability (KEV) catalog.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-26399, a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in the AjaxProxy component of SolarWinds Web Help Desk, to its Known Exploited Vulnerability (KEV) catalog.

author: Camaro Dragon (Chinese-nexus threat actor)
description: Researchers at Check Point reveal the Chinese-nexus threat actor Camaro Dragon attempted to deploy a variant of PlugX malware against Qatari targets within one day of the launch of Operation Epic Fury and the onset of the escalation in the Middle East

author: Chinese-nexus threat actor
description: Check Point Research observe another attack targeting Qatar and using a password-protected archive, likely delivered via email. The campaign employed low-quality AI-generated lures impersonating the Israeli government to deliver a previously unseen Rust-based loader.

author: APT 28 (a.k.a. Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard, Strontium, and Sednit)
description: Researchers at ESET reveal that the Russian state-sponsored APT28 threat group is using a custom variant of the open-source Covenant post-exploitation framework for long-term espionage operations.

author: “KadNap”
description: Researchers at Black Lotus Labs team at Lumen discover a sophisticated new malware named “KadNap,” primarily targeting Asus routers, conscripting them into a botnet that proxies malicious traffic. Since August 2025, we have been monitoring the growth of this network, which is now above 14,000 infected devices.

author: Unknown (likely a Brazilian-based cybercrime group)
target: Users of Brazilian financial institutions and cryptocurrency holders
description: Researchers at Kaspersky discover "BeatBanker," a dual-threat malware combining cryptocurrency mining with banking trojan capabilities. It targets Brazilian users by monitoring clipboards to hijack crypto transactions and using overlay windows to steal banking credentials, maximizing illicit profits through both resource exploitation and direct financial theft.

author: Russian-speaking threat actor
description: Researchers at Aryaka discover "BlackSanta," a sophisticated malware designed to disable Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) systems. This "EDR-killer" utilizes kernel-level exploits to terminate security processes, allowing ransomware or other payloads to operate undetected. It represents a significant escalation in defensive evasion techniques targeting enterprise security stacks.

author: ‘PhantomRaven’
target: Software developers and DevOps engineers using the npm registry
description: Researchers at Endor Labs detail the resurgence of the PhantomRaven campaign, with 88 new malicious npm packages belonging to three new waves, utilizing malicious npm packages to target developers.

author: Unknown
description: Starbucks discloses a data breach affecting hundreds of employees after threat actors gained access to their Starbucks Partner Central accounts, compromising 889 Starbucks Partner Central accounts used to manage employment details, personal information, benefits, and HR information.

author: Unknown (potential access attempts from Ukraine, Kazakhstan).
target: Organizations using FortiGate Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) appliances.
description: Researchers at Sentinel One discover a campaign where attackers exploited FortiGate firewall vulnerabilities to compromise corporate networks.

author: Unknown
target: Rust developers and Continuous Integration (CI) pipelines.
description: Researchers at Socket discover a supply chain attack involving five malicious Rust that exfiltrate .env files. These packages impersonated legitimate time utilities to steal developer secrets, such as API keys and database credentials, transmitting them to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Kaspersky discover BeatBanker, a sophisticated Android Trojan targeting Brazilian users. It employs a dual-threat approach, combining a cryptocurrency miner with the BTMOB banking Trojan.

author: Homeland Justice
description: Albania’s parliament says that it had been targeted by a “sophisticated” cyberattack aimed at deleting data and compromising several internal systems.

author: Unknown
target: Visitors of legitimate WordPress websites (250+ identified) and Windows users globally (specifically targeting digital wallets and credentials).
description: Researchers at Rapid7 Labs analyze an ongoing campaign where over 250 legitimate WordPress websites were compromised to host fake Cloudflare CAPTCHAs. These "ClickFix" lures trick users into executing PowerShell commands that deliver multi-stage infostealers, including Vidar, Impure Stealer, and a new C++ variant called VodkaStealer, targeting credentials and digital wallets.

author: Unknown
target: Users and repositories utilizing the xygeni/xygeni-action@v5 GitHub Action (estimated at over 130 repositories).
description: Xygeni discovers a supply chain attack where compromised credentials were used to "poison" the v5 tag of their official GitHub Action. The attacker injected a command-and-control (C2) reverse shell, enabling arbitrary command execution.

author: Handala
description: Leading medical technology company Stryker is hit by a wiper malware attack claimed by Handala, an Iranian-linked and pro-Palestinian hacktivist group.

author: Unknown
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) orders government agencies to patch their systems against CVE-2025-68613, an actively exploited n8n vulnerability.

author: UNC6426
description: Researchers at Google Threat Intelligence Group reveal that a threat actor known as UNC6426 leveraged keys stolen following the supply chain compromise of the nx npm package last year to completely breach a victim's cloud environment within a span of 72 hours.

author: Unknown
target: Users of the PIX payment system and major Brazilian financial institutions
description: Researchers at Zimperium discover PixRevolution, an Android trojan exploiting accessibility services. It utilizes real-time screen monitoring and an operator-controlled injection model to hijack PIX transfers.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Sophos discover a ClickFix campaign that used OpenAI's ChatGPT Atlas web browser as bait, delivered via sponsored search results on Google, to direct users to a fake Google Sites URL with a download button that, when clicked, displayed instructions to open the Terminal app, paste a command to it, and downloaded a shell script, which prompts the user to enter the system password and runs MacSync with user-level permissions.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Sophos discover a malvertising campaign that leveraged sponsored links to lead users to shared conversations on the legitimate OpenAI ChatGPT redirecting victims to malicious GitHub-themed landing pages that tricked users into running malicious commands on the Terminal app.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Sophos discover a campaign targeting Belgium, India, and parts of North and South America that distributed a new variant of MacSync delivered through ClickFix lures. The latest iteration supports dynamic AppleScript payloads and in-memory execution to evade static analysis, bypass behavioral detections, and complicate incident response.
country: BE IN North America South America

author: Iran
description: Meta says it removed about 300 accounts and pages across Facebook and Instagram part of an influence operation linked to Iran that used “sophisticated fake personas” on Instagram to build relationships with U.S. users before introducing political messaging.

author: Medusa
description: Bell Ambulance, a prominent ambulance service in Milwaukee confirms that threat actors targeted their systems last year and stole sensitive information on more than 235,000 people.

author: Cl0p (linked to the threat cluster FIN11)
description: Michelin confirms a data breach following the widespread cybercrime campaign targeting Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) users. Attackers exploited a zero-day vulnerability to exfiltrate over 315 GB of data. Michelin stated the breach was localized and contained no sensitive or technical IT information, with no impact on its global operations.

author: Unknown
target: Child Exploitation Forensic Lab in the FBI’s New York Field Office
description: An unidentified foreign hacker broke into the FBI’s field office in New York in 2023 and compromised files related to the bureau’s investigation into the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

author: ShinyHunters
description: Canadian business process outsourcing giant Telus Digital confirms it suffered a security incident after threat actors claimed to have stolen nearly 1 petabyte of data from the company in a multi-month breach.

author: Interlock
description: Researchers at IBM X-Force discover a likely AI-generated novel malware, dubbed “Slopoly,” used during an Interlock ransomware attack.

author: AiLock
description: England Hockey, the governing body for field hockey in England, is investigating a potential data breach after the AiLock ransomware gang listed it as a victim on its data leak site. The threat actor allegedly stole 129GB of data from the organization’s systems.

author: Unknown
description: Loblaw Companies Limited (Loblaw), the largest food and pharmacy retailer in Canada, announces that threat actors breached a portion of its IT network and accessed basic customer information.

author: Unknown
description: Google releases emergency security updates to patch CVE-2026-3909 and CVE-2026-3910, two high-severity Chrome vulnerabilities exploited in zero-day attacks.

author: Storm-2561
target: Users searching for enterprise VPN software
description: Researchers at Microsoft reveal that a threat actor tracked as Storm-2561 is distributing fake enterprise VPN clients from Ivanti, Cisco, and Fortinet to steal VPN credentials from unsuspecting users.

author: Threat actors from Iran?
target: Poland’s National Centre for Nuclear Research (NCBJ)
description: Poland’s National Centre for Nuclear Research (NCBJ) says threat actors targeted its IT infrastructure, but the attack was detected and blocked before causing any impact.

author: 'byst4'
target: 33 financial institutions and digital asset platforms (including Itaú, Santander, Bradesco, Nubank, Binance, and Coinbase).
description: Researchers at ZenoX discover VENON, a sophisticated banking Trojan targeting Brazilian financial institutions. Unlike traditional Delphi-based malware, VENON is written entirely in Rust, utilizing AI-assisted "vibe coding" and advanced encryption to evade detection and automate financial theft.

author: CL-STA-1087 (suspected threat actor from China).
description: Researchers at Palo Alto Networks identify a long-term espionage campaign by Chinese-linked actor CL-STA-1087 targeting Southeast Asian military organizations. The attackers utilized custom backdoors, AppleChris and MemFun, to steal sensitive intelligence regarding military capabilities and collaborative efforts.

author: GlassWorm
target: Software developers and DevOps engineers using GitHub, npm, and VS Code
description: The GlassWorm supply-chain campaign returns with a new, coordinated attack that targets hundreds of packages, repositories, and extensions on GitHub, npm, and VSCode/OpenVSX extensions.

author: Russian-linked actors with potential links to Laundry Bear (a.k.a. UAC-0190 or Void Blizzard)
description: Researchers at Lab52 identify "DRILLAPP," a JavaScript-based backdoor targeting Ukraine. Linked to Russian actors (potentially Laundry Bear), the campaign uses judicial and charity-themed lures to infect systems via Edge. It leverages browser capabilities to record audio, capture screens, and access files, representing an evolving method for evading traditional detection.

author: Unknown
description: American robotic surgery giant Intuitive says that information from certain internal IT business applications was accessed by an unauthorized third party as the result of a targeted cybersecurity phishing incident.

author: GlassWorm
target: Hundreds of GitHub Python repositories and their maintainers/users (including Django apps, ML research, and PyPI packages)
description: Researchers at StepSecurity discover "ForceMemo," a sophisticated campaign where attackers use compromised credentials from malicious VS Code extensions to force-push malware into hundreds of GitHub Python repositories. The malware uses the Solana blockchain for command-and-control instructions and downloads Node.js to execute encrypted payloads, specifically avoiding Russian systems.

author: Payload
description: The Payload Ransomware group claims to have hacked the Royal Bahrain Hospital (RBH) and stolen 110 GB of data. The ransomware gang adds the healthcare facility to its Tor data leak site and published the images of allegedly hacked systems as proof of the attack.

description: Description
