author: Ukrainian Cyber Alliance
description: The Russian city of Perm restores its parking payment system after a cyberattack last week knocked the service offline and temporarily made parking free for several days.

author: Threat actors using the Kratos Phishing-as-a-Service Kit
target: C-level executive at security firm Outpost24
description: Researchers at SpecOps reveal the details of a sophisticated multi-chain redirect phishing campaign exploiting legitimate Cisco and Nylas domains to target a C-level executive at its parent company Outpost24

author: Unknown
target: Users of PayPal and Amazon (consumers and employees)
description: Researchers at Cofense reveal that phishers are weaponizing LiveChat, a legitimate SaaS support platform, to conduct real-time social engineering. Attackers use branded chat windows to impersonate Amazon or PayPal, tricking victims into sharing credentials, credit card details, and MFA codes through what appears to be a genuine customer service session.

author: Warlock (a.k.a. Water Manaul)
description: Researchers at Trend Micro examine an advanced campaign by the Warlock ransomware group were attackers exploited unpatched SharePoint servers, using Cloudflare tunnels for stealthy C&C, persistent BYOVD techniques to disable EDR, and Rclone for exfiltrating sensitive data before deploying ransomware.

author: LeakNet (a ransomware-as-a-service or ransomware group)
target: Multiple organizations including charitable organizations, manufacturing, healthcare, financial services, transportation, business services and consulting, insurance, sports and gaming, education, energy, architectural services, engineering services, and logistics sectors
description: Researchers at ReliaQuest identify a strategic shift by the LeakNet ransomware group toward self-directed initial access. By deploying "ClickFix" social engineering lures on compromised websites and utilizing a stealthy, in-memory Deno-based loader, the group has scaled its operations to bypass traditional file-based security controls across diverse global industries.

author: Unknown
target: Nordstrom customers and the company's email/communication infrastructure
description: Attackers abuse Nordstrom's official email system to send cryptocurrency scams to customers. Disguised as a St. Patrick's Day promotion," the emails promised a 200% return on deposits. The breach likely involved compromised Okta and Salesforce credentials, allowing legitimate infrastructure to distribute fraudulent messages.

author: APT28 (a.ka. Fancy Bear, Sednit, Strontium, Pawn Storm, Sofacy)
target: Ukrainian State Hydrology Agency (under the Ministry of Infrastructure)
description: Seqrite Labs discovers "Operation GhostMail," a Russian-linked APT campaign exploiting the Zimbra Webmail XSS vulnerability (CVE-2025-66376) to compromise a Ukrainian government agency. The attack uses obfuscated JavaScript embedded in a phishing email to exfiltrate credentials, 2FA codes, and 90 days of mailbox content via DNS and HTTPS.

author: Lazarus Group (a.k.a. Guardians of Peace, or Hidden Cobra).
description: Bitrefill attributes a recent infrastructure breach to North Korea’s Lazarus Group. After compromising an employee’s laptop, attackers drained hot wallets, exploited gift card inventory, and stole 18,500 purchase records. The company identified the state-sponsored group through malware analysis, on-chain tracing, and reused IP addresses.

author: Konni (an APT group often linked to North Korean interests)
target: South Korean individuals and organizations, including North Korean human rights activists, lecturers, and psychological counselors.
description: Researchers at Genians analyze a multi-stage campaign by the Konni APT group targeting South Korean individuals. Using North Korea-themed spear-phishing, the attackers deployed remote access malware via malicious LNK files. They hijacked victims' KakaoTalk accounts to distribute secondary malware to contacts, leveraging established trust to expand the infection.

author: WaterPlum (part of the Contagious Interview Campaign from North Korea)
target: Developers and professionals involved in blockchain-related projects.
description: Researchers from NTT Security Japan discover that WaterPlum shifted to a new modular malware named "StoatWaffle." The group uses deceptive VSCode configurations in repositories to trick users into executing malicious code, which then downloads Node.js modules to steal browser credentials and gain remote access.

author: Unknown
description: The educational services company Kaplan notifies state regulators that 1.4 million people had Social Security and driver’s license numbers leaked following a cybersecurity incident in the fall of 2025.

author: Unknown
target: Video gamers seeking "free cheats" for major titles
description: Researchers at Acronis identify a widespread campaign distributing Vidar Stealer 2.0 through hundreds of fraudulent GitHub repositories and Reddit posts. Masquerading as free game cheats, the malware exfiltrates sensitive browser data, cryptocurrency wallets, and Azure tokens from unsuspecting gamers.

author: UNC6353
description: Researchers at Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reveal that UNC6353, a suspected Russian espionage actor, has been using the Coruna exploit kit since July 2025, and in December 2025 started leveraging the new DarkSword iOS exploits against Ukrainian targets.

author: UNC6748
description: Researchers at Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reveal that UNC6748 was the first threat actor using the DarkSword iOS exploit kit in attacks targeting Saudi Arabian users via a website impersonating Snapchat.

author: Threat actors associated with PARS Defense
description: Researchers at Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) says that in late November 2025, DarkSword was used in Turkey, in activity associated with PARS Defense, a Turkish commercial surveillance vendor, on devices running iOS 18.4-18.7.

author: Threat actors associated with PARS Defense
description: Researchers at Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) notice the DarkSword being used in Malaysia by another PARS Defense customer delivering the GHOSTSABER backdoor.

author: Interlock
target: Multiple organizations in the Education, Manufacturing, Healthcare, and Public administration
description: Researchers at Amazon discover a campaign by the Interlock ransomware group exploiting a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-20131) in Cisco’s Management Center software.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: CISA orders U.S. government agencies to secure their servers against CVE-2025-66376, an actively exploited vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS).

author: ShinyHunters
description: Identity protection company Aura confirms that an unauthorized party gained access to nearly 900,000 records containing names and email addresses.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: CISA warns that CVE-2026-20963, a critical Microsoft SharePoint vulnerability patched in January is now being exploited in attacks.

author: Threat actors from Iran?
description: CISA warns U.S. organizations to follow Microsoft guidance to strengthen the Intune endpoint management tool after the cyberattack that exploited it to wipe medical technology giant Stryker's systems.

author: Unknown
description: Navia Benefit Solutions, Inc. (Navia) informs nearly 2.7 million individuals of a data breach that exposed their sensitive information to attackers.

author: Unknown
target: Developers on GitHub, specifically those who "starred" or interacted with OpenClaw-related repositories
description: Researchers at OX Security discover a phishing campaign targeting developers with fake token allocations. Attackers created malicious GitHub issues, tagging users to lure them to a cloned openclaw.ai site. The site contained obfuscated JavaScript (eleven.js) designed to connect to and drain various crypto wallets (MetaMask, Trust Wallet, etc.).

author: Unknown
target: Financial institutions in Turkey and Italy, as well as crypto services
description: Researchers at ThreatFabric discover "Perseus," an advanced Android malware evolving from the Phoenix and Cerberus families. It specializes in Device Takeover (DTO) by abusing Accessibility Services to perform overlay attacks, keylogging, and a unique "scan_notes" feature that systematically steals sensitive information from note-taking applications like Google Keep and Evernote.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) orders federal agencies to patch a maximum-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-20131, in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) by Sunday, March 22.

author: Threat actors using the VoidStealer MaaS (Malware-as-a-Service)
target: Users of Chromium-based browsers (Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge) on Windows systems
description: Researchers at Gen Digital discover "VoidStealer," a novel MaaS infostealer that bypasses Google Chrome’s Application-Bound Encryption (ABE).

author: Unknown
description: Mazda Motor Corporation (Mazda) announces that information belonging to its employees and business partners had been exposed in a security incident detected last December.

author: 'Runningcrab'
target: Organizations and individuals using Cobra DocGuard
description: Researchers at Symantec and Carbon Black discover "Speagle," a stealthy infostealer targeting users of Cobra DocGuard security software. The malware hijacks legitimate infrastructure for command-and-control, exfiltrating sensitive data, while masking its activity as normal client-server communication to evade detection.

author: Unknown
target: Organizations using Quest KACE Systems Management Appliance (SMA)
description: Researchers at Arctic Wolf reveal that threat actors are suspected to be exploiting CVE-2025-32975, a maximum-severity security flaw impacting Quest KACE Systems Management Appliance (SMA).

author: Unknown
target: Multiple organizations including financial services, education, information technology (IT), insurance, and healthcare, primarily in the United States
description: Researchers at Microsoft discover a campaign that was delivering the Energy365 PhaaS phishing kit and used tax and Certified Public Accountant (CPA) lures throughout the attack chain.

author: Unknown
target: Approximately 100 organizations, in the manufacturing, retail, and healthcare primarily in the United States
description: Researchers at Microsoft discover tax-themed phishing emails containing an attachment redirecting to a phishing page built with the SneakyLog PhaaS platform and mimicking the Microsoft 365 sign-in page to steal credentials.

author: Unknown
target: Wide range of industries primarily in the United States
description: Researchers at Microsoft discover a campaign with several hundred emails containing a link redirecting to a domain distributing the remote management and monitoring (RMM) tool ScreenConnect.

author: Unknown
target: Multiple organizations in the U.S., primarily higher education
description: Researchers at Microsoft discover a campaign impersonating the US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) with a cryptocurrency lure, and distributing the remote management and monitoring (RMM) tool ScreenConnect.

author: Unknown
target: Multiple accounting companies and few related industries such as financial services, legal, and insurance in the U.S.
description: Researchers at Microsoft discover a campaign targeting CPAs, asking for assistance in filing taxes, asking for a quote, and typically providing a backstory, and distributing the remote management and monitoring (RMM) tool Datto.

author: Unknown
target: Multiple organizations in the U.S. including financial services, technology and software, and retail and consumer goods
description: Researchers at Microsoft observe a large-scale phishing campaign sent to more than 29,000 users across 10,000 organizations, impersonating the the IRS, and distributing the remote management and monitoring (RMM) tool ScreenConnect.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Blackpoint identify RoadK1ll, a Node.js-based malware designed for internal network pivoting. Using custom WebSocket framing, it establishes a reverse tunnel to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

author: Unknown
target: Thousands of Magento-based e-commerce sites, including global brands (Toyota, FedEx, ASUS, Lindt), government services, and Trump Organization domains.
description: Researchers at Netcraft identify a massive campaign defacing approximately 15,000 hostnames on 7,500 Magento domains. Attackers uploaded plaintext files to global brands and government services, primarily to build reputation within the defacement subculture through mass opportunistic exploitation.

author: WorldPay
description: Los Angeles Metro says it's working to restore access to its internal administrative computers after the agency's security team discovered "unauthorized activity." The WorldPay ransomware group claims responsibility for the attack.

author: Unknown attacker using the PureLog Stealer Malware-as-a-Service)
description: Researchers at Trend Micro discover a campaign targeting industries in Germany, Canada, the US, and Australia via social engineering with language-specific legal lures to trick users into executing files that launch a complex, fileless infection chain to steal credentials and crypto-wallets.

author: Russian intelligence-linked threat actors
target: Individuals of high intelligence value, such as current and former U.S. government officials, military personnel, political figures, and journalists
description: The FBI issues a public service announcement warning that Russian intelligence-linked threat actors are actively targeting users of encrypted messaging apps such as Signal and WhatsApp in phishing campaigns that have already compromised thousands of accounts.

author: TeamPCP
target: Users of the Aqua Security Trivy scanner
description: The Trivy vulnerability scanner is compromised in a supply-chain attack by threat actors known as TeamPCP, which distributed credential-stealing malware through official releases and GitHub Actions.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: CISA orders U.S. government agencies to patch CVE-2025-31277, CVE-2025-43510, and CVE-2025-43520, the three iOS vulnerabilities targeted in cryptocurrency theft and cyberespionage attacks using the DarkSword exploit kit.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: CISA orders U.S. government agencies to patch CCVE-2025-54068, a code injection vulnerability in Laravel Livewire, currently exploited in the wild.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: CISA orders U.S. government agencies to patch CVE-2025-32432, a code injection vulnerability in Craft CMS, currently exploited in the wild.

author: Iranian-linked and pro-Palestinian Handala hacktivist group
description: The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) warns that Iranian threat actors linked to the country's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS) are using Telegram in malware attacks.

author: Operators of the Tycoon2FA Phishing-as-a-Service platform
target: Users of Microsoft 365 and Google cloud environments globally.
description: Researchers at CrowdStrike reveal that the Tycoons 2FA, a Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) platform is persisting following the March 2026 law enforcement takedown of 330 domains. Despite the disruption, the platform quickly rebounded, using Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) techniques to bypass MFA and maintaining high volumes of cloud account compromises.

author: Unknown
description: Foster City, California is forced to pause all public services outside of emergency responses in light of a ransomware attack.

author: Unknown
description: Trio-Tech International, a semiconductor testing company warns regulators that its subsidiary in Singapore suffered a ransomware attack.

author: Unknown
description: A cyberattack on vehicle breathalyzer company Intoxalock disables backend calibration systems, stranding thousands of US drivers with court-mandated ignition interlocks. The disruption prevents mandatory maintenance, locking vehicles and highlighting the risks of centralized, internet-connected automotive safety infrastructure.

author: Unknown
description: Heritage Bank discloses that threat actors copied files from an internal employee file-sharing server. The stolen data includes employees’ and customers’ private and confidential information, such as names, Social Security numbers, account numbers, dates of birth, and addresses.

author: Unknown
description: A "callback phishing" campaign abuses Microsoft’s Azure Monitor alert system. Attackers create malicious alert rules in Azure tenants to send legitimate-looking notification emails. These messages bypass security filters to deliver fraudulent billing lures, ultimately tricking victims into calling attacker-controlled phone numbers for social engineering.

author: TeamPCP
target: Users of the Aqua Security Trivy scanner
description: Researchers at Aikido Security identify a destructive TeamPCP campaign using "CanisterWorm" malware to target Kubernetes clusters. The malware fingerprints systems; those identified as Iranian via timezone or locale are wiped using a "kamikaze" DaemonSet, while others receive a persistent backdoor disguised as PostgreSQL monitoring tools.

author: TeamPCP
target: Kubernetes clusters and Docker APIs, specifically targeting systems located in Iran for destruction.
description: Researchers at Check Point reveal a surge in attempts to compromise internet-connected surveillance cameras across the Middle East during the ongoing regional conflict, with activity attributed to infrastructure linked to Iranian threat actors.
country: IL QA BH KW AE LB

author: TeamPCP
target: Aqua Security (specifically their Trivy container scanning tool and GitHub organization).
description: Researchers at Socket reveal that compromised Trivy Docker images (0.69.4–0.69.6) were pushed to Docker Hub, bypassing GitHub releases. These images contained "TeamPCP" infostealer malware, utilizing a typosquatted C2 domain for exfiltration. The breach targeted Aqua Security’s supply chain, potentially affecting numerous downstream CI/CD pipelines and third-party integrations using automated updates.

author: Unknown
description: Decentralized finance platform Resolv reveals that a cyberattack allowed a threat actor to compromise the company’s infrastructure and illicitly create $80 million worth of its USR stablecoin.

author: Unknown
description: Popular anime streaming platform Crunchyroll is investigating a breach after hackers claimed to have stolen personal information for approximately 6.8 million people.

author: Unknown
description: The Dutch Ministry of Finance confirms that some of its systems were breached in a cyberattack detected last week.

author: Unknown
description: Bug bounty platform HackerOne notifies hundreds of employees that their data was stolen after attackers hacked Navia, one of its U.S. benefits administrators.

author: TeamPCP
description: Researchers at Sysdig discover that TeamPCP expanded its supply chain attack from Aqua Security’s Trivy to Checkmarx’s GitHub Actions. By harvesting credentials from CI/CD runner memory, the actor poisoned multiple trusted actions, exfiltrating encrypted secrets to vendor-specific typosquatted domains.

author: EvilTokens Phishing as a Service
description: Researchers at Huntress discover a large-scale campaign where attackers use Railway.com’s infrastructure to conduct device code phishing. Victims are tricked into entering authentication codes on legitimate Microsoft endpoints, allowing attackers to harvest OAuth tokens, bypass MFA, and maintain persistent access to corporate environments.

author: Unknown
description: Hightower Holding, the parent company of financial management services provider Hightower Advisors, notifies over 130,000 individuals of a data breach.

author: LAPSUS$
description: The LAPSUS$ group claims to have breached AstraZeneca, leaking nearly 3GB of internal data including source code, cloud infrastructure details (AWS/Azure), and employee records. Initially offered for sale, the archive was later released for free.

author: Nasir Security
description: Researchers at Resecurity discover a relatively new cybercriminal group called Nasir Security, presumably associated with Iran, that is targeting energy organizations in the Middle East.

author: Nasir Security
description: Researchers at Resecurity discover a relatively new cybercriminal group called Nasir Security, presumably associated with Iran, that is targeting energy organizations in the Middle East.

author: Nasir Security
description: Researchers at Resecurity discover a relatively new cybercriminal group called Nasir Security, presumably associated with Iran, that is targeting energy organizations in the Middle East.

author: Unknown
target: Developers (seeking AI/Docker tools), gamers (Roblox, Fishing Planet), and crypto users
description: Researchers at Netskope identify a massive "malware factory" using AI-generated lures to target developers and gamers. The campaign distributes trojanized GitHub repositories and 300+ packages, employing a two-component LuaJIT design to evade sandboxes and exfiltrate desktop screenshots and credentials.

author: ShinyHunters
description: Infinite Campus, a widely used K-12 student information system, warns customers of a data breach following an extortion attempt by the threat actor ShinyHunters. The threat actor compromised an employee’s Salesforce account via a sophisticated "vishing" campaign, exfiltrating staff contact details and directory information. The company refused ransom demands.

author: TeamPCP
description: Researchers at Endor Labs discover a supply chain attack by "TeamPCP" targeting the litellm Python library. Attackers published backdoored versions (1.82.7, 1.82.8) to PyPI containing a credential harvester, Kubernetes lateral movement toolkit, and a persistent systemd backdoor, targeting developers and cloud environments to exfiltrate secrets and SSH keys.

author: Russian-speaking threat actor
target: General internet users, specifically targeting those using cryptocurrency wallets (728 extensions) and password managers (103 extensions)
description: Researchers at Gen Digital researchers unmask "Torg Grabber," a sophisticated information-stealing malware-as-a-service. Initially disguised as Vidar malware, it evolved rapidly from Telegram-based exfiltration to a professional REST API infrastructure. It employs multi-layered obfuscation and "ClickFix" lures to steal credentials from over 850 browser extensions, focusing heavily on cryptocurrency wallets.

author: Unknown
target: Employees and organizations using Microsoft services
description: Researchers at Kaspersky identify a phishing campaign leveraging the "Bubble" no-code app builder to create malicious web applications. These apps, hosted on legitimate Bubble servers, bypass security filters by using complex, auto-generated code to redirect users to fraudulent Microsoft sign-in pages designed to steal corporate credentials.

author: Unknown
target: An unnamed multinational car manufacturer, along with other e-commerce stores using Adobe Commerce/Magento.
description: Researchers at Sansec discover a payment skimmer targeting the ‘PolyShell’ vulnerability in version 2 of Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce installations. It bypasses Content Security Policy (CSP) and traditional HTTP-based defenses by using WebRTC DataChannel, to load its malicious payload and exfiltrate stolen credit card data directly to the attacker's server.

author: 'mikilanjillo'
target: Software developers (specifically those using React and crypto-related tools) and cryptocurrency wallets
description: Researchers at ReversingLabs discover the "Ghost campaign". The attack employs malicious npm packages that display fake installation logs to hide activity and phish for sudo passwords. Once obtained, these passwords are used to install a RAT that steals sensitive data and crypto assets.

author: Unnamed financially-motivated threat actor
target: French-speaking corporate and enterprise environments (specifically HR and recruitment staff).
description: Researchers at Securonix uncover "FAUX#ELEVATE," a campaign targeting French enterprises with fake CV-themed VBScript droppers. Using extreme obfuscation and domain-join checks, it deploys a multi-purpose toolkit including XMRig cryptominers and infostealers. The attack exploits legitimate services like Dropbox and compromised WordPress sites to exfiltrate credentials and maximize illicit profits.

author: Pay2Key
description: A U.S. healthcare organization is targeted by Pay2Key, an Iranian ransomware gang with ties to the country’s government.

author: Unknown
description: Healthcare management services provider QualDerm Partners notifies more than 3.1 million people that their personal, medical, and health insurance information was stolen in a December 2025 data breach.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Palo Alto Networks reveal the details of sophisticated phishing campaigns where attackers impersonate Palo Alto Networks talent acquisition staff. These attacks specifically target senior-level professionals by leveraging scraped LinkedIn data to craft highly personalized lures.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warns that threat actors are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability identified as CVE-2026-33017, which affects the Langflow framework for building AI agents.

author: Unknown
description: Dutch professional football club Ajax Amsterdam (AFC Ajax) discloses that a threat actor exploited vulnerabilities in its IT systems and accessed data belonging to a few hundred people.

author: Unknown
description: The Dutch National Police (Politie) says a security breach resulting from a successful phishing attack has had a limited impact and hasn't affected citizens' data.

author: Unknown
target: Software developers and maintainers on GitHub, specifically those using Visual Studio Code
description: Researchers at Socket identify a massive phishing campaign using fake GitHub Discussions to broadcast "critical" Visual Studio Code vulnerability alerts. Attackers trick developers into downloading malicious "updates" from external links, using a redirection chain to fingerprint user systems and deliver follow-on malware or exploit kits.

author: Bearlyfy (a.k.a Labubu)
target: Organizations in Russia, including large-scale enterprises
description: Researchers at F6 detail the evolution of the pro-Ukrainian hacking group "Bearlyfy" (also known as Labubu). Since January 2025, they have executed over 70 attacks on Russian businesses, transitioning from using leaked ransomware like LockBit 3 to developing their own custom malware, "GenieLocker," to maximize financial and operational damage.

author: Silver Fox (a.k.a. Void Arachne or SwimSnake)
target: Chinese-speaking users, specifically those seeking VPNs, encrypted messengers (Signal, Telegram), and cryptocurrency tools.
description: Researchers at Hexastrike reveal that the Chinese-nexus threat actor Silver Fox (Void Arachne) deployed the AtlasCross RAT by impersonating trusted software like VPNs and messengers. Using typosquatted domains and stolen EV code-signing certificates, the multi-stage campaign employs fileless execution and the PowerChell framework to exfiltrate data and hijack RDP sessions while evading security products.

author: Unknown
description: Puerto Rico’s Department of Transportation is forced to cancel all upcoming appointments at the agency that handles driver’s licenses, permits and vehicle registrations due to a cyberattack.

author: Unknown
description: A ransomware attack disrupts digital systems at Spain’s Port of Vigo, forcing authorities to disconnect parts of its network and temporarily manage cargo operations manually.

author: North Korean APT groups (overlapping with "Contagious Interview")
target: Undisclosed organizations in the retail industry
description: Researchers at eSentire’s discover EtherRAT, a Node.js-based backdoor linked to North Korean actors. The malware uses "EtherHiding" via Ethereum smart contracts to secure C2 addresses, targeting the retail sector through ClickFix and IT support scams to exfiltrate data.

author: Infiniti Stealer
description: Researchers at Malwarebytes identify "Infiniti Stealer," a novel macOS infostealer, employing "ClickFix" social engineering, tricking users into pasting malicious Terminal commands from fake CAPTCHA pages. The malware is written in Python and compiled with Nuitka into a native binary to evade detection while exfiltrating credentials, crypto wallets, and keychain data.

author: Red Menshen (a.k.a. Earth Bluecrow, DecisiveArchitect, and Red Dev 18)
target: Global Telecommunications networks (specifically mobile operators and signaling systems) and Government entities
description: Researchers at Rapid7 Labs discover a long-term espionage campaign by a China-linked threat actor using the BPFDoor malware. "Digital sleeper cells" are embedded within global telecommunications backbones to monitor government communications, track subscriber data, and maintain persistent, kernel-level access across 4G and 5G networks.
country: Multiple countries (primarily targets in the Middle East and Asia)

author: Unknown
target: Marketing teams and business users managing TikTok for Business and Google Ad Manager accounts
description: Researchers at Push Security discover a sophisticated phishing campaign targeting "TikTok for Business" and Google accounts. Attackers use "Adversary-in-the-Middle" (AITM) kits to steal session tokens, bypassing MFA. These compromised accounts are typically exploited for malvertising scams, ad fraud, and distributing further malware via trusted business profiles.

author: Stately Taurus (a.k.a. Mustang Panda)
target: Undisclosed government organization in Southeast Asia
description: Researchers at Palo Alto Networks reveal the details of cyber espionage campaign by the Chinese threat actor Stately Taurus targeting a government organization in Southeast Asia via the USB-propagated malware called USBFect (aka HIUPAN), which deploys a PUBLOAD backdoor.

author: CL-STA-1048 (overlapping with Earth Estries and those behind the Crimson Palace)
target: Undisclosed government organization in Southeast Asia
description: During the same activity, researchers at Palo Alto Networks discover an additional campaign against the same organization using a toolkit of espionage payloads, deploying multiple RATs like MasolRAT and the RawCookie backdoor.

author: CL-STA-1049 (overlapping with Unfading Sea Haze)
target: Undisclosed government organization in Southeast Asia
description: During the same activity, researchers at Palo Alto Networks discover an additional campaign against the same organization showing stealth and persistence, with attackers using the novel Hypnosis loader to deploy the FluffyGh0st RAT. This activity overlaps with the China-aligned group known as Unfading Sea Haze.

author: TA446 (a.k.a. Star Blizzard, Callisto, ColdRiver, SeaBorgium)
description: Researchers at Proofpoint reveal that the Russian state-sponsored group tracked as Star Blizzard has adopted the DarkSword iOS exploit kit in an ongoing campaign.

author: ShinyHunters
description: The European Commission is investigating a data breach after a threat actor compromised an Amazon Web Services account. The threat actor claimed to exfiltrate over 350 GB of data, including employee information and databases. Few days later the European Commission confirms the breach claimed by the ShinyHunters group.

author: TeamPCP
target: Developers and organizations using the Telnyx Python SDK
description: Attackers from TeamPCP hijack the popular Telnyx Python SDK on PyPI to distribute credential-stealing malware. The attack utilized steganography to hide malicious code within WAV audio files. The malware targets SSH keys, cloud tokens, and Kubernetes secrets across Linux, macOS, and Windows systems.

author: Unnamed threat actors
description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds CVE-2025-53521, a critical security flaw impacting F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.

author: Unknown
description: Security researchers from multiple company observe massive reconnaissance activity for CVE-2026-3055, a recently disclosed critical security flaw impacting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway. Few days later the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) orders government agencies to patch their Citrix NetScaler appliances.

author: Qilin (a.k.a. Agenda)
description: The German political party Die Linke suffers a severe cyberattack targeting its IT infrastructure. Upon discovery, the party isolates systems to prevent data theft. The incident was later linked to the Qilin ransomware group.

author: Unknown
description: Healthcare IT firm CareCloud discloses a data breach incident that exposed sensitive data and caused a network disruption lasting approximately eight hours.

author: Russia
target: Public opinion in Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia
description: Latvia’s Defense Ministry says that Russia is carrying out a coordinated disinformation campaign against Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia, falsely claiming that the Baltic states are allowing their territories to be used for Ukrainian attacks on Russia.

author: UAC-0255
target: State organizations, medical centers, security companies, educational institutions, financial institutions, and software development companies in Ukraine
description: The Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) discloses details of a new phishing campaign in which the cybersecurity agency itself was impersonated to distribute a remote administration tool known as AGEWHEEZE.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Defused warn that threat actors are now actively exploiting CVE-2026-21643, a critical vulnerability in Fortinet's FortiClient EMS platform.

author: Handala
target: Personal email account of FBI Director Kash Patel
description: The Handala threat actors associated with Iran breach the personal email account of FBI Director Kash Patel and publish photos and documents. The FBI has confirmed the compromise, saying that the stolen data was not recent and did not include any government data.

author: Unknown
target: General enterprise environments and corporate users
description: Researchers at ReliaQuest identify "DeepLoad," a malware using AI-generated obfuscation and "ClickFix" social engineering to compromise enterprise environments.

author: UNC1069
target: The Axios npm package (and by extension, the millions of developers and automated CI/CD systems that download it)
description: Researchers at StepSecurity reveal that attackers compromised the Axios npm package by hijacking the lead maintainer's account to publish malicious versions 1.14.1 and 0.30.4. Few days later Google formally attributes the supply chain compromise to a financially motivated North Korean threat activity cluster tracked as UNC1069.

author: 'eviltokensadmin'
description: Researchers at Sekoia uncover "EvilTokens," a sophisticated Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) kit targeting Microsoft 365. It uses device code phishing to bypass MFA, harvesting access/refresh tokens. The platform includes AI-powered automation for email harvesting and reconnaissance, enabling large-scale Business Email Compromise (BEC) attacks across various sectors.

author: TeamPCP
target: Users of Trivy (Aqua Security), KICS (Checkmarx), LiteLLM, and Telnyx projects/packages
description: TeamPCP leveraged credentials stolen from Trivy, KICS, and LiteLLM supply chain attacks to infiltrate cloud environments. They rapidly validated secrets using TruffleHog, conducted AWS/GitHub reconnaissance, and exfiltrated massive datasets.

author: Qilin (a.k.a. Agenda)
description: The Qilin ransomware group claims to have breached the chemical manufacturing giant Dow Inc, after adding the company to its Tor data leak site.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Proofpoint observe a campaign impersonating the U.S. IRS. The lure purported to relate to the target’s recent IRS filing.

author: TA4922
description: Researchers at Proofpoint discover a TA4922 campaign targeting organizations in Japan with emails impersonating national tax authorities and claiming the recipient had unresolved tax obligations.

author: TA4922
description: Researchers at Proofpoint discover another TA4922 campaign targeting Japan and purporting to be from the "Inland Revenue Department." Messages include a URL which downloaded an executable, which, if executed, installed an information stealer

author: TA2730
description: Researchers at Proofpoint reveal the details of a campaign carried out by the threat actor TA2730, targeting Switzerland and Canada.

author: Unknown
description: Researchers at Proofpoint reveal the details of a campaign impersonating company executives, human resources, or vendor/supplier contacts in attempts to steal financial and personal data, likely with a goal of leveraging it for follow-on fraud.

author: Chinese-nexus threat actor (linked to aliases/frameworks like Amaranth Dragon and ShadowPad)
description: Check Point Research identify "Operation TrueChaos," a targeted espionage campaign exploiting a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-3502) in the TrueConf video conferencing platform. Attackers compromised on-premises servers to distribute malicious updates to government entities in Southeast Asia, ultimately deploying the Havoc post-exploitation framework for reconnaissance and data theft.

target: Android mobile device users (specifically those using older/unpatched OS versions)
description: Researchers at McAfee discover "Operation NoVoice," an Android rootkit campaign infecting 2.3 million devices via 50+ Google Play apps. The malware uses polyglot images and hardware-specific exploits to gain root access, inject code into apps like WhatsApp, and survive factory resets. It primarily targets older, unpatched Android versions in developing regions.
